units.zh: 安重榮，朔州人。
units.en: An Chongrong was a native of Shuozhou.
units.literal: An Chongrong was a man of Shuozhou.

units.zh: 祖從義，利州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Congyi had served as prefect of Lizhou.
units.literal: His grandfather Congyi was Governor of Lizhou.

units.zh: 父全，勝州刺史、振武蕃漢馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: His father Quan had been prefect of Shengzhou and commander of all Han and tribal horse and foot forces at Zhenwu.
units.literal: His father Quan was Governor of Shengzhou and Commander-in-Chief of the Han and foreign cavalry and infantry of Zhenwu.

units.zh: 重榮有膂力，善騎射。
units.en: Chongrong was powerfully built and excelled at riding and archery.
units.literal: Chongrong had great physical strength and was skilled at mounted archery.

units.zh: 唐長興中，為振武道巡邊指揮使，犯罪下獄。
units.en: During the Tang Changxing period he served as frontier patrol commander on the Zhenwu circuit, but after committing an offense he was thrown into prison.
units.literal: In the Changxing era of Tang he served as frontier patrol commander on the Zhenwu circuit, committed an offense, and was imprisoned.

units.zh: 時高行周為帥，欲殺之，其母赴闕申告，樞密使安重誨陰護之，張敬達之圍晉陽也，高祖聞重榮在代北，使人誘之，重榮乃召邊士，得千騎赴焉。
units.en: Gao Xingzhou was then in command and meant to execute him, but Chongrong's mother appealed at court, and the Commissioner of Military Affairs An Chonghui shielded him in secret. When Zhang Jingda besieged Jinyang, Gaozu learned that Chongrong was in northern Dai and sent envoys to recruit him; Chongrong rallied border soldiers and came with a thousand horsemen.
units.literal: At that time Gao Xingzhou was military governor and wished to kill him; his mother went to court to plead her case, and the Commissioner of Military Affairs An Chonghui secretly protected him. When Zhang Jingda besieged Jinyang, Emperor Gaozu heard that Chongrong was in northern Dai and sent men to win him over; Chongrong then summoned border troops and mustered a thousand horsemen to join him.

units.zh: 高祖大喜，誓以土地。
units.en: Gaozu was overjoyed and swore to reward him with land.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and pledged him territory.

units.zh: 及即位，授成德軍節度使，累加至使相。
units.en: After his enthronement he made Chongrong military governor of Chengde and eventually elevated him to commissioner and chief minister.
units.literal: When he took the throne, he appointed him Military Governor of the Chengde army and repeatedly promoted him until he reached the rank of commissioner-minister.

units.zh: 自梁、唐已來，藩侯郡牧，多以勛授，不明治道，例為左右群小惑亂，賣官鬻獄，割剝蒸民，率有貪猥之名，其實賄賂半歸於下。
units.en: Since the Liang and Tang dynasties, most frontier lords and prefects had won their posts through merit rather than learning how to govern; they were typically led astray by petty hangers-on, sold offices and verdicts, and squeezed the people. Nearly all bore a name for greed, though in truth half the bribes went to their underlings.
units.literal: Since Liang and Tang, regional lords and prefects had mostly been appointed for merit, did not understand governance, and were routinely misled by petty followers around them, selling offices and judgments, stripping the common people—almost all had a reputation for greedy misconduct, though in fact half the bribes went to subordinates.

units.zh: 惟重榮自能鉤距，凡有爭訟，多廷辯之，至於倉庫耗利，百姓科徭，悉入於己，諸司不敢窺覬。
units.en: Chongrong alone kept his own accounts sharp: he usually heard disputes in open court, and warehouse profits, popular levies, and corvée labor all flowed into his coffers while no subordinate office dared even look askance.
units.literal: Only Chongrong himself could investigate and reckon; whenever there was litigation he often heard cases in open court, and as for warehouse surpluses, levies on the people, and corvée—all went into his own purse, and no office dared covet them.

units.zh: 嘗有夫婦共訟其子不孝者，重榮面加詰責，抽劍令自殺之，其父泣曰：「不忍也。」
units.en: Once a couple brought suit together against their son for unfilial conduct. Chongrong rebuked the youth in person, drew his sword, and told him to take his own life. The father wept and said, "I cannot bring myself to do it."
units.literal: Once a husband and wife jointly sued their son for unfilial conduct; Chongrong rebuked him to his face, drew his sword, and ordered the son to kill himself; the father wept and said, "I cannot bear it."

units.zh: 其母詬詈，仗劍逐之。
units.en: His mother cursed him and, brandishing the sword, chased him to do it.
units.literal: His mother reviled him and, sword in hand, drove him on.

units.zh: 重榮疑而問之，乃其繼母也，因叱出，自後射之，一箭而斃，聞者莫不快意。
units.en: Chongrong questioned them in suspicion and learned she was the stepmother. He drove her out, then shot her from behind with a single arrow and killed her on the spot. Everyone who heard of it felt vindicated.
units.literal: Chongrong grew suspicious and questioned them; she turned out to be his stepmother, so he shouted her out, then shot her from behind—one arrow and she was dead; all who heard of it were delighted.

units.zh: 由此境內以為強明，大得民情。
units.en: Thereafter the people within his jurisdiction took him for stern and discerning, and he won broad popular approval.
units.literal: From this the realm within his borders regarded him as stern and clear-sighted, and he greatly won popular sentiment.

units.zh: 重榮起於軍伍，暴得富貴，復睹累朝自節鎮遽升大位，每謂人曰：「天子，兵強馬壯者當為之，寧有種耶！」
units.en: Chongrong had come up through the army and suddenly acquired wealth and rank. He had also watched dynasty after dynasty vault from regional command straight to the throne, and he would say to people, "Whoever has the strongest troops and horses ought to be Son of Heaven—does the office run in families?"
units.literal: Chongrong had risen from the ranks and suddenly gained wealth and rank; he also saw how successive dynasties had swiftly advanced from military governors to the throne, and he often told people, "The Son of Heaven ought to be whoever has the strongest soldiers and horses—is there a breed for it?"

units.zh: 又以奏請過當，為權臣所否，心常憤憤，遂畜聚亡命，收市戰馬，有飛揚跋扈之志。
units.en: His petitions had also grown excessive and were rejected by the power-holders at court, so resentment festered in him. He began stockpiling outlaws, buying war-horses, and nursing an arrogant, rebellious ambition.
units.literal: Moreover, because his memorial requests were excessive and were denied by powerful ministers, his heart was constantly resentful; he then gathered fugitives, bought war-horses on the market, and harbored an overbearing, defiant ambition.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：帝之遣重榮代秘瓊也，戒之曰：「瓊不受代，當別除汝一鎮，勿以力取，恐為患滋深。」
units.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: When the emperor dispatched Chongrong to replace Mi Qiong, he cautioned him: "If Qiong refuses to step down, we will appoint you to another circuit instead. Do not seize it by force, or the trouble will only deepen."
units.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: When the emperor sent Chongrong to replace Mi Qiong, he warned him, saying, "If Qiong refuses to yield his post, you will be given another commandery—do not take it by force, lest the trouble grow worse."

units.zh: 重榮由是以帝為怯，謂人曰：「秘瓊匹夫耳，天子尚畏之，況我以將相之重、士民之眾乎！」）〉
units.en: From this Chongrong concluded the emperor was timid and said to others, "Mi Qiong is only a commoner, yet the Son of Heaven still fears him—what of me, with the rank of general and minister and armies and people at my back?")〉
units.literal: Chongrong therefore took the emperor for timid and told people, "Mi Qiong is a mere commoner, yet the Son of Heaven still fears him—how much more so for me, with the weight of general and minister and the multitude of soldiers and people!" )〉

units.zh: 嘗因暴怒殺部校賈章，以謀叛聞。
units.en: Once, in a violent rage, he executed his subordinate officer Jia Zhang on a charge of plotting rebellion.
units.literal: Once in a fit of rage he killed his subordinate officer Jia Zhang on a report of plotting rebellion.

units.zh: 章有女一人，時欲舍之，女曰：「我家三十口，繼經兵亂，死者二十八口，今父就刑，存此身何為？」
units.en: Zhang had a daughter. When he meant to spare her, she said, "Our family numbers thirty souls; war after war has left twenty-eight dead. Now my father is to die—why should I go on living?"
units.literal: Zhang had one daughter; at the time he wished to spare her, but the daughter said, "Our household has thirty mouths; through successive wars twenty-eight have died; now my father is to be executed—what is the use of keeping this body alive?"

units.zh: 再三請死，亦殺之。
units.en: She begged again and again to die, and he killed her too.
units.literal: She repeatedly begged for death, and he killed her as well.

units.zh: 鎮人由是惡重榮之酷，而嘉賈女之烈焉。
units.en: The garrison populace thereafter detested Chongrong's cruelty while honoring Jia's daughter for her fierce loyalty.
units.literal: The people of the commandery therefore hated Chongrong's cruelty but praised the daughter of Jia for her stern resolve.

units.zh: 天福中，朝廷姑息契丹，務安邊塞，重榮每見蕃使，必以箕踞慢罵。
units.en: During the Tianfu reign the court indulged the Khitan and sought only to keep the frontier quiet. Whenever Chongrong met Khitan envoys he would sit with legs sprawled and revile them.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era the court indulged the Khitan and strove to secure the frontier; whenever Chongrong saw Khitan envoys he invariably sat sprawled and insulted them with contempt.

units.zh: 會有美棱數十騎由其境內，交言不遜，因盡殺之，契丹主大怒，責讓朝廷。
units.en: Once several dozen Meiling horsemen passed through his territory and spoke insolently; he had them all killed. The Khitan ruler was enraged and laid blame on the court.
units.literal: It happened that several dozen riders of Meiling passed through his territory; their words were insolent, so he killed them all; the Khitan ruler was furious and reproached the court.

units.zh: 朝廷隱忍，未即加罪，重榮乃密構吐渾等諸族，以為援助，上表論之。
units.en: The court swallowed the insult and did not punish him at once. Chongrong then secretly enlisted the Tuguhun and other tribes as allies and memorialized the throne on the matter.
units.literal: The court swallowed the affront and did not immediately punish him; Chongrong then secretly rallied the Tuguhun and other tribes as support and submitted a memorial setting forth his case.

units.zh: 其略曰：
units.en: The gist of the memorial ran as follows:
units.literal: The gist of it read:

units.zh: 臣昨據熟吐渾節度使白承福、赫連公德等，各領本族三萬餘帳，自應州地界奔歸王化。
units.en: Your servant has lately received Bai Chengfu, Helian Gede, and other settled Tuguhun military governors, each leading more than thirty thousand tents of their tribes, who fled from the Yingzhou frontier to submit to the throne.
units.literal: Your servant has lately received the settled Tuguhun military governors Bai Chengfu, Helian Gede, and others, each leading more than thirty thousand tents of their own tribes, who fled from the Yingzhou border back to imperial civilization.

units.zh: 續準生吐渾並渾葜兩突厥三部落，南北將沙陀、安慶、九府等，各領部族老小，並牛羊、車帳、甲馬，七八路慕化歸奔，俱至五臺及當府地界已來安泊。
units.en: After them came the raw Tuguhun together with the Hunqie and two Turkic tribes, and the northern and southern commanders of the Shatuo, Anqing, Jiufu, and others, each bringing their people, young and old, with cattle, sheep, wagons, tents, armor, and horses. Seven or eight columns in all have come to submit; all have reached Wutai and the borders of this prefecture and are now encamped.
units.literal: Thereafter the raw Tuguhun together with the Hunqie and two Turkic tribes, the northern and southern commanders Shatuo, Anqing, Jiufu, and others, each leading their tribes old and young together with cattle, sheep, carts, tents, armor, and horses—seven or eight routes in all came admiring civilization to submit; all have reached Wutai and the borders of this commandery and are now settled.

units.zh: 累據告勞，具說被契丹殘害，平取生口，率略羊馬，淩害至甚。
units.en: They have repeatedly reported their hardships, describing in full how the Khitan have brutalized them—seizing people at will, driving off flocks and herds, and oppressing them beyond measure.
units.literal: Repeatedly they have reported their hardships, fully describing how they have been cruelly harmed by the Khitan, who seize captives at will, drive off sheep and horses, and oppress them to an extreme degree.

units.zh: 又自今年二月後來，須令點檢強壯，置辦人馬衣甲，告報上秋向南行營，諸蕃部等實恐上天不祐，殺敗後隨例不存家族，所以預先歸順，兼隨府族，各量點檢強壯人馬約十萬眾。
units.en: Since the second month of this year they have also been ordered to muster the able-bodied and equip men, horses, clothing, and armor, with word that they will march south in the autumn campaign. The tribes truly fear Heaven will not favor them and that, once defeated, their families will be wiped out as usual. They have therefore submitted in advance; together with the tribes attached to this prefecture, they have mustered roughly one hundred thousand able-bodied men and horses.
units.literal: Moreover, since the second month of this year they have been ordered to muster the able-bodied, prepare men, horses, clothing, and armor, and have been told that in the coming autumn they will campaign south; the various tribal groups truly fear that Heaven will not aid them and that after defeat their clans will perish as usual, so they have submitted in advance; together with the tribes following this prefecture, each has mustered able-bodied men and horses to a total of about one hundred thousand.

units.zh: 又準沿河党項及山前、山後、逸利、越利諸族部落等首領，並差人各將契丹所授官告、職牒、旗號來送納，例皆號泣告勞，稱被契丹淩虐，憤惋不已，情願點集甲馬，會合殺戮。
units.en: The chieftains of the Tangut along the river and of the tribes of the fore-mountains, rear-mountains, Yili, Yueli, and others have each sent envoys bearing the commissions, patents, and banners the Khitan gave them to hand them over. All weep as they report their hardships, saying the Khitan have abused them beyond endurance; they are eager to muster armor and horses and join in the slaughter.
units.literal: Moreover, the chieftains of the Tangut along the river and of the tribes before the mountains, behind the mountains, Yili, Yueli, and others have each sent men bearing the commissions, credentials, and banners conferred by the Khitan to surrender them; all weep and report their hardships, saying they have been abused by the Khitan and are ceaselessly indignant, and wish to muster armor and horses to join in slaughtering them.

units.zh: 續又朔州節度副使趙崇與本城將校殺偽節度使劉山，尋已安撫軍城，乞歸朝廷。
units.en: Moreover, Zhao Chong, deputy military governor of Shuozhou, and the city's officers have killed the puppet military governor Liu Shan, pacified the garrison city, and beg to return to the court.
units.literal: Furthermore, the deputy military governor of Shuozhou Zhao Chong and the garrison officers of the city killed the false military governor Liu Shan; the army city has already been pacified and they beg to return to the court.

units.zh: 臣相次具奏聞。
units.en: Your servant has reported these matters in successive memorials.
units.literal: Your servant has reported all this in successive memorials.

units.zh: 昨奉宣頭及累傳聖旨，令臣凡有往復契丹，更須承奉，當候彼生頭角，不欲自起釁端，貴守初終，不愆信誓。
units.en: Yesterday I received the imperial rescript and repeated sacred instructions that in all dealings with the Khitan I must continue to defer to them, wait until they show their mettle, not provoke trouble myself, and above all keep faith from start to finish without breaking our sworn pledges.
units.literal: Yesterday I received the imperial rescript and repeated sacred instructions ordering your servant that in all dealings with the Khitan I must continue to serve them, wait until they grow horns, not wish to raise trouble myself, and value keeping the beginning and end intact without breaking sworn faith.

units.zh: 仰認睿旨，深惟匿瑕，其如天道人心，至務勝殘去虐，須知機不可失，時不再來。
units.en: I bow to acknowledge the sage intent and ponder deeply the need to overlook faults, yet Heaven's way and men's hearts alike demand that cruelty be overcome and oppression removed. Opportunity cannot be missed, and time will not return.
units.literal: I bow to acknowledge the sage intent and deeply ponder concealing flaws, yet as to the Way of Heaven and the hearts of men, the utmost task is to overcome cruelty and remove oppression; one must know that opportunity cannot be lost and time does not come again.

units.zh: 竊以諸蕃不招呼而自至，朔郡不攻伐以自歸，蓋系人情，盡由天意。
units.en: I venture to think that the tribes came without being summoned and Shuozhou returned without being attacked—surely this reflects the people's will and Heaven's intent alike.
units.literal: I venture to think that the various tribes came without being summoned and Shuozhou returned without being attacked—this surely reflects human sentiment and is wholly Heaven's will.

units.zh: 更念諸陷蕃節度使等，本自勛勞，早居富貴，沒身邊塞，遭酷虐以異常，企足朝廷，冀傾輸而不已，如聞傳檄，盡願倒戈。
units.en: I further recall the military governors trapped under Khitan rule—men who earned their rank by merit, rose early to wealth, and spent their lives on the frontier, only to suffer cruelty beyond measure. They strain toward the court and long to pour out their loyalty without end; if they hear a proclamation, all will turn their blades.
units.literal: I further recall the various military governors trapped under the Khitan, who originally won merit, long enjoyed wealth and rank, spent their lives on the frontier, and suffered cruelty beyond the norm; they strain toward the court, hoping to pour out their loyalty without cease; if they hear a proclamation, all wish to turn their blades.

units.zh: 如臣者雖是愚蒙，粗知可否，不思忌諱，罄寫丹衷，細具敷陳，冀裨萬一。
units.en: Though your servant is dull, I roughly know what can and cannot be done. Without regard for taboo I lay bare my loyal heart in full detail, hoping to be of some small use.
units.literal: Though your servant is dull and ignorant, I roughly know what may or may not be done; without regard for taboo I have fully written my loyal heart and set forth the details in hope of aiding even one part in ten thousand.

units.zh: 其表數千言，大抵指斥高祖稱臣奉表，罄中國珍異，貢獻契丹，淩虐漢人，竟無厭足。
units.en: The memorial ran to several thousand characters and largely denounced Gaozu for submitting as a vassal, draining China's rare treasures as tribute to the Khitan, and abusing the Han people without end.
units.literal: The memorial ran to several thousand characters and largely denounced Emperor Gaozu for submitting as a vassal, exhausting China's rare treasures in tribute to the Khitan, and abusing the Han people without ever being satisfied.

units.zh: 又以此意為書，遺諸朝貴及藩鎮諸侯。
units.en: He also set out this argument in letters sent to court nobles and regional lords alike.
units.literal: He also made this intent into letters and sent them to the court nobles and the various regional lords.

units.zh: 高祖憂其變也，遂幸鄴都以詔諭之，凡有十焉。
units.en: Gaozu feared rebellion and went in person to Yedu to admonish him by edict in ten points.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu feared he would rebel and therefore went in person to Yedu to admonish him by edict; there were ten points in all.

units.zh: 其略曰：「爾身為大臣，家有老母，忿不思難，棄君與親。
units.en: The gist ran: "You are a great minister with an aged mother at home, yet in anger you refuse to weigh the cost and abandon both your sovereign and your kin.
units.literal: The gist read: "You are a great minister and have an aged mother at home; in anger you do not consider difficulty and abandon your lord and kin.

units.zh: 吾因契丹而興基業，爾因吾而致富貴，吾不敢忘，爾可忘耶！
units.en: I built my foundation through the Khitan; you grew rich and noble through me. I dare not forget that—can you?
units.literal: I rose to my foundation through the Khitan; you grew rich and noble through me—I dare not forget; can you forget?

units.zh: 且前代和親，只為安邊，今吾以天下臣之，爾欲以一鎮抗之，大小不等，無自辱焉。」
units.en: Former dynasties made marriage alliances only to secure the frontier. Now I have made the whole realm their vassal, while you would resist them with a single circuit—the scales do not match. Do not bring shame on yourself."
units.literal: Moreover, in former ages marriage alliances were only to secure the frontier; now I have made the whole realm their vassal, while you wish to resist them with one commandery—the great and small are unequal; do not disgrace yourself."

units.zh: 重榮愈恣縱不悛，雖有此奏，亦密令人與契丹幽州帥劉晞結托。
units.en: Chongrong grew ever more defiant and unrepentant. Despite the memorial, he also secretly sent men to ally with Liu Xi, the Khitan commander at Youzhou.
units.literal: Chongrong grew ever more unrestrained and unrepentant; though he had this memorial, he also secretly sent men to ally with Liu Xi, Khitan commander of Youzhou.

units.zh: 蓋重榮有內顧之心，契丹幸我多事，復欲侵吞中國，契丹之怒重榮，亦非本誌也。
units.en: Chongrong had his own domestic concerns; the Khitan welcomed our troubles and again meant to swallow China. Their anger at Chongrong was not their original aim either.
units.literal: For Chongrong had misgivings at home; the Khitan rejoiced in our many troubles and again wished to swallow China—the Khitan anger at Chongrong was not their original intent either.

units.zh: 時重榮嘗與北來蕃使並轡而行，指飛鳥射之，應弦而落，觀者萬眾，無不快抃，蕃使因輟所乘馬以慶之，由是名振北方，自謂天下可以一箭而定也。
units.en: Once Chongrong rode alongside envoys from the north, pointed at birds in flight, and brought them down at the twang of his bow. Tens of thousands of spectators cheered. The envoys gave up their mounts to congratulate him. His fame thereafter shook the north, and he told himself the realm could be settled with a single arrow.
units.literal: At that time Chongrong once rode side by side with envoys coming from the north, pointed at flying birds and shot them—they fell at the twang of the string; tens of thousands of onlookers all clapped with delight; the envoys therefore gave up the horses they rode to congratulate him; from this his fame shook the north, and he himself said the realm could be settled with a single arrow.

units.zh: 又重榮素與襄州安從進連結，及聞從進將議起兵，而奸謀乃決。
units.en: Chongrong had long been allied with An Congjin of Xiangzhou. When he heard Congjin was about to raise troops, his treacherous plot was finally set.
units.literal: Moreover, Chongrong had long been linked with An Congjin of Xiangzhou; when he heard Congjin was about to discuss raising troops, his treacherous plot was finally settled.

units.zh: 天福六年冬，大集境內饑民，眾至數萬，揚旌向闕，聲言入覲。
units.en: In the winter of the sixth Tianfu year he gathered the hungry within his borders until they numbered tens of thousands, raised banners toward the capital, and claimed he was coming to court.
units.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Tianfu he massed the hungry people within his borders to a multitude of tens of thousands, raised banners toward the capital, and declared he was coming to court.

units.zh: 朝廷遣杜重威帥師禦之，遇於宗城。
units.en: The court sent Du Chongwei at the head of an army to meet him, and they clashed at Zongcheng.
units.literal: The court sent Du Chongwei to command troops against him; they met at Zongcheng.

units.zh: 軍才成列，有賊將趙彥之臨陣卷旗來奔。
units.en: The armies had barely formed when the rebel general Zhao Yanzhi furled his banner on the field and defected.
units.literal: The armies had just formed their lines when the rebel general Zhao Yanzhi rolled up his banner on the field and came over in surrender.

units.zh: 重榮方戰，聞彥之背己，大恐，退於輜重中，王師因而擊之，一鼓而潰。
units.en: Chongrong was fighting when he learned Yanzhi had turned on him. Terrified, he fell back among the baggage train. The imperial army struck at once and routed him in a single assault.
units.literal: Chongrong was in the midst of battle when he heard Yanzhi had turned against him; he was greatly afraid and withdrew among the baggage train; the imperial army then struck, and at one drumbeat his force collapsed.

units.zh: 重榮與十餘騎北走，其下部眾，屬嚴冬寒冽，殺戮及凍死者二萬餘人。
units.en: Chongrong fled north with a dozen riders. Of his followers, in the depths of bitter winter, more than twenty thousand were slain or froze to death.
units.literal: Chongrong fled north with a dozen horsemen; of his followers, in the depth of bitter winter cold, more than twenty thousand were killed in battle or froze to death.

units.zh: 重榮至鎮，取牛馬革旋為甲，使郡人分守夾城以待王師。
units.en: Chongrong returned to his prefecture, stripped hides from cattle and horses to improvise armor, and had the people man the inner and outer walls in shifts to await the imperial army.
units.literal: Chongrong returned to his commandery, took ox and horse hides and quickly made armor, and had the people of the prefecture man the twin walls in shifts to await the imperial army.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·解暉傳》：安重榮反鎮州，因舉兵向闕，至宗城，晉師逆戰，大破之。
units.en: (Song History, biography of Jie Hui: When An Chongrong rebelled at Zhenzhou and marched on the capital, the Jin army met him at Zongcheng and broke him utterly.)
units.literal: (Song History, biography of Jie Hui: An Chongrong rebelled at Zhenzhou and raised troops toward the capital; reaching Zongcheng, the Jin army met him in battle and routed him utterly.)

units.zh: 暉募軍中壯士百餘人，夜搗賊壘，殺獲甚眾。
units.en: Hui recruited more than a hundred stalwarts from the army and raided the rebel camp by night, killing and capturing a great many.
units.literal: Hui recruited more than a hundred stalwarts from the army and at night raided the rebel camp, killing and capturing a great many.

units.zh: 暉頻中流矢，而督戰自若，顏色不撓，以功遷列校。）〉
units.en: Though struck by arrows again and again, Hui directed the fight as calmly as ever, his face unshaken, and was promoted to company commander for his merit.)〉
units.literal: Hui was repeatedly struck by stray arrows yet directed battle as calmly as ever, his expression unshaken, and was promoted to company commander for his merit.)〉

units.zh: 杜重威至，有部將自西郭水門引官軍入焉，殺守陴百姓萬餘人，重威尋害導者，自收其功。
units.en: When Du Chongwei arrived, a subordinate led the imperial army in through the West Guo water gate, killing more than ten thousand townspeople who defended the walls. Chongwei soon killed the guide and claimed the credit himself.
units.literal: When Du Chongwei arrived, a subordinate led the imperial army in through the West Guo water gate, killing more than ten thousand common people defending the walls; Chongwei soon killed the guide and claimed the credit himself.

units.zh: 重榮擁吐渾數百，匿於牙城，重威使人襲而得之，斬首以進。
units.en: Chongrong had several hundred Tuguhun with him hidden in the headquarters city. Chongwei sent men to seize him, beheaded him, and presented the head.
units.literal: Chongrong had several hundred Tuguhun with him hidden in the headquarters city; Chongwei sent men to strike and seize him, beheaded him, and presented the head.

units.zh: 高祖禦樓閱其俘馘，宣露布訖，遣漆其頭顱，函送契丹。
units.en: Gaozu mounted the tower to review the captive and the severed heads. After the victory bulletin was proclaimed, he had the skull lacquered and sent it in a box to the Khitan.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu mounted the tower to review the captive and severed heads; after proclaiming the victory bulletin, he had the skull lacquered and sent in a box to the Khitan.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：安重榮出鎮，常懷不軌之計久矣，但未發。
units.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: After An Chongrong took up his command, he had long nursed rebellious designs but had not yet acted.)
units.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: After An Chongrong went out to his command, he had long harbored disloyal designs but had not yet acted.)

units.zh: 居無何，廄中產朱鬃白馬，黑鴉生五色雛，以為鳳，乃欣然謂天命在己，遂舉兵反。
units.en: Before long his stables produced a white horse with a red mane, and a black crow hatched five-colored chicks. Taking this for a phoenix omen, he joyfully declared Heaven's mandate was his and raised troops in rebellion.
units.literal: Before long, in the stables a white horse with a red mane was born and a black crow hatched five-colored chicks; taking them for a phoenix, he gladly said Heaven's mandate was his and then raised troops in rebellion.

units.zh: 指揮令取宗嶺路以向闕。
units.en: He ordered his army to take the Zongling road toward the capital.
units.literal: He ordered his command to take the Zongling route toward the capital.

units.zh: 時父老聞之，往往竊議曰：「事不諧矣，且王姓安氏，曰鞍得背而穩，何不取路貝州？
units.en: When the elders heard, they whispered among themselves: "This will not succeed. The king's surname is An, and they say a saddle is steady when it has a back—why not take the road through Beizhou?
units.literal: When the elders heard this they often whispered among themselves, saying, "The affair will not succeed; moreover the king's surname is An—one says a saddle is steady when it has a back—why not take the road through Beizhou?

units.zh: 若由宗嶺，是鞍及於鬃，得無危乎！」
units.en: If he goes by Zongling, the saddle reaches the mane—is that not perilous?"
units.literal: If one goes by Zongling, the saddle reaches the mane—is there not danger?"

units.zh: 未幾，與王師先鋒遇，一戰而敗。）〉
units.en: Before long he met the imperial vanguard and was broken in a single battle.)〉
units.literal: Before long he met the vanguard of the imperial army and was defeated in a single battle.)〉

units.zh: 安從進。
units.en: An Congjin.
units.literal: An Congjin.

units.zh: （《歐陽史》：從進，其先索葛部人也。
units.en: (Ouyang's History: Congjin's ancestors were of the Suoge tribe.
units.literal: (Old History of the Five Dynasties: Congjin's ancestors were of the Suoge tribe.

units.zh: 初事莊宗為護駕馬軍都指揮使，領貴州刺史，明宗時為保義彰武軍節度使。
units.en: At first he served Zhuangzong as commander of the palace-guard cavalry, held Guizhou as prefect, and under Mingzong was military governor of Baoyi and Zhangwu.
units.literal: At first he served Zhuangzong as commander of the palace-guard cavalry, held the post of prefect of Guizhou, and under Mingzong was military governor of Baoyi and Zhangwu.

units.zh: 湣帝即位，徙領順化。
units.en: When Emperor Min took the throne he was transferred to command Shunhua.
units.literal: When Emperor Min took the throne he was transferred to command Shunhua.

units.zh: 清泰中，徙鎮山南東道。
units.en: During Qingtai he was transferred to command Shannan East Circuit.
units.literal: During Qingtai he was transferred to command Shannan East Circuit.

units.zh: 晉高祖即位，加同中書門下平章事。）
units.en: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he was made Acting Chief Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.)
units.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he was made Acting Chief Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.)

units.zh: 天福六年，高祖幸鄴，討安重榮。
units.en: In the sixth Tianfu year Gaozu went to Ye to campaign against An Chongrong.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu Gaozu went to Ye to campaign against An Chongrong.

units.zh: 少帝以鄭王留守京師，時和凝請於高祖曰：「陛下北征，臣料安從進必反，何以制之？」
units.en: Emperor Shaodi had the Prince of Zheng remain at the capital. He Ning then petitioned Gaozu, saying, "Your Majesty is campaigning north. I expect An Congjin will certainly rebel. How can he be controlled?"
units.literal: Emperor Shaodi had the Prince of Zheng remain at the capital. At that time He Ning petitioned Gaozu, saying, "Your Majesty is campaigning north. I expect An Congjin will certainly rebel. How are we to control him?"

units.zh: 高祖曰：「卿意將奈何？」
units.en: Gaozu said, "What do you propose?"
units.literal: Gaozu said, "What do you propose?"

units.zh: 凝曰：「臣聞之兵法，先人者奪人。
units.en: Ning said, "I have heard in the art of war that he who strikes first seizes the initiative from others.
units.literal: Ning said, "I have heard in the art of war that he who strikes first seizes the initiative from others.

units.zh: 願陛下為空名宣敕十通授鄭王，有急則命將往。」
units.en: I beg Your Majesty to prepare ten blank imperial edicts and give them to the Prince of Zheng, so that in an emergency he may commission generals to go."
units.literal: I beg Your Majesty to prepare ten blank imperial edicts and give them to the Prince of Zheng, so that in an emergency he may commission generals to go."

units.zh: 從進聞高祖往北，遂反，少帝以空名授李建崇、郭金海討之。
units.en: When Congjin heard Gaozu had gone north he rebelled. Shaodi used blank commissions to appoint Li Jianchong and Guo Jinhai to suppress him.
units.literal: When Congjin heard Gaozu had gone north he rebelled. Shaodi used blank commissions to appoint Li Jianchong and Guo Jinhai to suppress him.

units.zh: 從進引兵攻鄧州，不克，進至湖陽，遇建崇等，大駭，以為神速，復為野火所燒，遂大敗，從進自焚。
units.en: Congjin led troops against Dengzhou but failed to take it. Advancing to Huyang he met Jianchong and the others, was greatly alarmed, took their speed for supernatural swiftness, and was again burned by wildfire. Utterly defeated, Congjin burned himself to death.
units.literal: Congjin led troops to attack Dengzhou but could not take it. Advancing to Huyang he met Jianchong and the others, was greatly alarmed, took their speed for supernatural swiftness, and was again burned by wildfire. He was utterly defeated and Congjin burned himself to death.

units.zh: 張彥澤，其先出於突厥，後為太原人也。
units.en: Zhang Yanze's ancestors came from the Turks and later became men of Taiyuan.
units.literal: Zhang Yanze's ancestors came from the Turks and later became men of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 祖、父世為陰山府裨將。
units.en: His grandfather and father for generations were deputy generals of Yinshan Prefecture.
units.literal: His grandfather and father for generations were deputy generals of Yinshan Prefecture.

units.zh: 彥澤少有勇力，目睛黃而夜有光色，顧視若鷙獸焉。
units.en: Yanze in youth had courage and strength. His eyes were yellow and at night gave off a luminous glow; when he turned his gaze he seemed like a fierce beast.
units.literal: Yanze in youth had courage and strength; his eyes were yellow and at night gave off a luminous color; when he turned his gaze he seemed like a fierce beast.

units.zh: 以騎射事後唐莊宗、明宗，以從戰有功，繼領郡守。
units.en: With riding and archery he served Later Tang's Zhuangzong and Mingzong. For meritorious service in battle he successively held prefectures.
units.literal: With riding and archery he served Later Tang's Zhuangzong and Mingzong; for meritorious service in battle he successively held prefectures.

units.zh: 高祖即位，擢為曹州刺史。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was promoted to prefect of Caozhou.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was promoted to prefect of Caozhou.

units.zh: 從楊光遠圍範延光於鄴，以功授華州節度使，尋移鎮涇州，累官至檢校太保。
units.en: Following Yang Guangyuan in besieging Fan Yanguang at Ye, he was made military governor of Huazhou for his achievements, soon transferred to command Jingzhou, and rose to Acting Grand Guardian.
units.literal: Following Yang Guangyuan in besieging Fan Yanguang at Ye, for his achievements he was made military governor of Huazhou, soon transferred to command Jingzhou, and rose to Acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 有從事張式者，以宗人之分，受其知遇。
units.en: There was an aide named Zhang Shi who, as a kinsman, had won his favor and trust.
units.literal: There was an aide named Zhang Shi who, as a clansman, received his favor and trust.

units.zh: 時彥澤有子為內職，素不葉父意，數行笞撻，懼其楚毒，逃竄外地，齊州捕送到闕，敕旨釋罪，放歸父所。
units.en: Yanze had a son in inner palace service who never pleased him and was repeatedly flogged. Fearing the beatings, the youth fled. Qizhou captured him and sent him to court, where an imperial order pardoned him and returned him to his father.
units.literal: At that time Yanze had a son in inner service who never pleased his father; he was repeatedly flogged, feared the cruel beatings, and fled to distant places; Qizhou captured and sent him to court; an imperial order pardoned him and returned him to his father.

units.zh: 彥澤上章，請行朝典，式以有傷名教，屢諫止之。
units.en: Yanze memorialized the throne asking for the full court punishment. Shi, saying it would violate ritual propriety, repeatedly urged him to desist.
units.literal: Yanze submitted a memorial requesting the full court punishment; Shi, because it would harm ritual propriety, repeatedly remonstrated to stop him.

units.zh: 彥澤怒，引弓欲射之，式僅而獲免。
units.en: Yanze flew into a rage, drew his bow to shoot him, and Shi barely escaped with his life.
units.literal: Yanze was angry, drew his bow intending to shoot him, and Shi barely escaped.

units.zh: 尋令人逐式出衙。
units.en: Soon he sent men to drive Shi out of headquarters.
units.literal: Soon he sent men to drive Shi out of the yamen.

units.zh: 式自為賓從，彥澤委以庶務，左右群小惡之久矣，因此讒構，互來迫脅，云：「書記若不便出，斷定必遭屠害。」
units.en: Shi had long served as a client and Yanze entrusted routine affairs to him. The petty hangers-on had hated him for years and now slandered him, pressing him in turn: "If the secretary does not leave at once, he will surely be killed."
units.literal: Shi had long served as a guest-follower and Yanze entrusted him with routine affairs; the petty followers around him had hated him for a long time and therefore slandered him, coming one after another to coerce him, saying, "If the secretary does not leave at once, he will surely be slaughtered."

units.zh: 式乃告病尋醫，攜其妻子將奔衍州。
units.en: Shi then pleaded illness to seek treatment, gathered his wife and children, and prepared to flee to Yanzhou.
units.literal: Shi then pleaded illness to seek a physician, took his wife and children, and was about to flee to Yanzhou.

units.zh: 彥澤遣指揮使李興領二十騎追之，戒曰：「張式如不從命，即斬取頭來。」
units.en: Yanze sent Commander Li Xing with twenty horsemen in pursuit and warned him: "If Zhang Shi does not obey, cut off his head and bring it back."
units.literal: Yanze sent the commander Li Xing with twenty horsemen in pursuit and warned him, saying, "If Zhang Shi does not obey, cut off his head and bring it back."

units.zh: 式懇告刺史，遂差人援送到汾州。
units.en: Shi earnestly appealed to the prefect, who sent men to escort him to Fenzhou.
units.literal: Shi earnestly appealed to the prefect, who then sent men to escort him to Fenzhou.

units.zh: 節度使李周驛騎以聞，朝廷以姑息彥澤之故，有敕流式於商州。
units.en: Military Governor Li Zhou reported by courier. Because the court indulged Yanze, an edict exiled Shi to Shangzhou.
units.literal: The military governor Li Zhou reported by relay horse; because the court indulged Yanze, there was an edict exiling Shi to Shangzhou.

units.zh: 彥澤遣行軍司馬鄭元昭詣闕論請，面奏云：「彥澤若不得張式，恐致不測。」
units.en: Yanze sent his campaigning marshal Zheng Yuanzhao to court to press the matter. He memorialized in person: "If Yanze does not get Zhang Shi, I fear unforeseen consequences."
units.literal: Yanze sent his campaigning marshal Zheng Yuanzhao to court to argue the request; he memorialized in person, saying, "If Yanze does not obtain Zhang Shi, I fear unforeseen consequences."

units.zh: 高祖不得已而從之。
units.en: Gaozu had no choice but to comply.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu had no choice but to comply.

units.zh: 既至，決口割心，斷手足而死之。
units.en: When Shi arrived, he cut open his mouth and heart, severed his limbs, and killed him.
units.literal: When Shi arrived, he cut open his mouth and heart, severed his limbs, and killed him.

units.zh: 式父鐸詣闕訴冤，朝廷命王周代之。
units.en: Shi's father Duo appealed at court for justice, and the court ordered Wang Zhou to replace Yanze.
units.literal: Shi's father Duo went to court to plead his wrong; the court ordered Wang Zhou to replace him.

units.zh: 周至任，奏彥澤在郡惡跡二十六條，逃散五千餘戶。
units.en: When Zhou took office, he memorialized twenty-six counts of Yanze's crimes in the prefecture and reported that more than five thousand households had fled.
units.literal: When Zhou took up his post, he memorialized twenty-six counts of Yanze's wicked deeds in the commandery and that more than five thousand households had fled.

units.zh: 彥澤既赴闕，刑法官李濤等上章請理其罪，高祖下制，止令削奪一階一爵而已，時以為失刑。
units.en: After Yanze came to court, the penal officials Li Tao and others memorialized asking that his crimes be tried. Gaozu issued an edict stripping only one rank and one title—a judgment widely regarded as a failure of justice.
units.literal: After Yanze came to court, the penal officials Li Tao and others submitted memorials requesting that his crimes be tried; Emperor Gaozu issued an edict stripping only one rank and one title—at the time this was regarded as a failure of justice.

units.zh: 少帝即位，桑維翰復舉之，尋出鎮安陽。
units.en: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne, Sang Weihan recommended him again, and he was soon sent out to command Anyang.
units.literal: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne, Sang Weihan again recommended him, and soon he went out to command Anyang.

units.zh: 既至，折節於士大夫，境內稱理，旋命領軍北屯恒、定。
units.en: Once there he humbled himself before scholar-officials, and the prefecture was said to be well governed. Soon he was ordered to lead troops north to garrison Heng and Ding.
units.literal: Once he arrived he humbled himself before scholar-officials; within his borders he was called orderly, and soon he was ordered to lead troops north to garrison Heng and Ding.

units.zh: 時易州地孤，漕運不繼，制令邢、魏、相、衛飛免以輸之，百姓荷擔累累於路，彥澤每援之以行，見羸困者，使其部眾代而助之。
units.en: Yizhou was then isolated and grain transport had broken down. The court ordered Xing, Wei, Xiang, and Wei to supply it by forced transport. The people bore loads in endless lines along the roads. Yanze often helped them along, and when he saw the weak and exhausted he had his troops carry the loads for them.
units.literal: At that time Yizhou was isolated and grain transport could not continue; an order commanded Xing, Wei, Xiang, and Wei to supply it by corvée transport; the people bore loads in endless lines along the roads; Yanze often lent them a hand as they went, and when he saw the weak and exhausted he had his troops take over and help.

units.zh: 洎至北邊，不令百姓深入，即遣騎士以馬負糧而去，往來既速，且無邀奪之患，聞者嘉之。
units.en: When he reached the northern border he kept the people from going deep into hostile territory and sent horsemen to carry grain on horseback instead. Transport was swift and free of robbery, and those who heard of it praised him.
units.literal: When he reached the northern border he did not let the common people go deep in; he immediately sent horsemen to carry grain away on horseback; the coming and going was swift and there was no trouble of robbery on the road; those who heard praised him.

units.zh: 陽城之戰，彥澤之功出於諸將之右，其後與敵接戰，頻獻捷於闕下，咸謂其感高祖不殺之恩，補昔年之過也。
units.en: At the battle of Yangcheng, Yanze's merit stood above the other generals. Thereafter, in repeated engagements with the enemy, he reported victory after victory to court. All said he was repaying Gaozu's grace in sparing his life and making amends for his past crimes.
units.literal: At the battle of Yangcheng, Yanze's merit stood above the other generals; afterward in engagements with the enemy he frequently reported victories to the court; all said he was moved by Gaozu's grace in sparing his life and was making up for his past faults.

units.zh: 開運三年冬，契丹既南牧，杜重威兵次瀛州。
units.en: In the winter of the third Kaiyun year the Khitan drove south, and Du Chongwei's army halted at Yingzhou.
units.literal: In the winter of the third year of Kaiyun the Khitan had already driven their herds south; Du Chongwei's army halted at Yingzhou.

units.zh: 彥澤為契丹所啖，密已變矣。
units.en: Yanze had been won over by the Khitan and had already turned in secret.
units.literal: Yanze had been won over by the Khitan and had secretly already turned.

units.zh: 乃通款於契丹，請為前導，因促騎說重威，引軍沿滹水西援常山，既而與重威通謀。
units.en: He opened relations with the Khitan and offered to serve as guide, then sent swift riders to persuade Chongwei to march west along the Hutuo to relieve Changshan. Soon he was in conspiracy with Chongwei.
units.literal: He then opened relations with the Khitan and asked to serve as guide; he sent swift riders to persuade Chongwei to lead the army west along the Hutuo to relieve Changshan, and soon conspired with Chongwei.

units.zh: 及王師降於中渡，契丹主遣彥澤統二千騎趨京師，以制少帝，且示公卿兆民以存撫之意。
units.en: When the imperial army surrendered at Zhongdu, the Khitan ruler sent Yanze at the head of two thousand horsemen to rush the capital, control Emperor Shaodi, and show court and people alike an intent to preserve and comfort them.
units.literal: When the imperial army surrendered at Zhongdu, the Khitan ruler sent Yanze at the head of two thousand horsemen to hurry to the capital to control Emperor Shaodi and also to show the court nobles and the myriad people an intent to preserve and comfort them.

units.zh: 彥澤以是歲十二月十六日夜，自封丘門斬關而入，以兵圜宮城。
units.en: On the night of the sixteenth day of the twelfth month that year, Yanze broke through the Fengqiu gate and entered, surrounding the palace with troops.
units.literal: On the night of the sixteenth day of the twelfth month of that year Yanze cut through the gate at Fengqiu and entered, surrounding the palace with troops.

units.zh: 翌日，遷帝於開封府舍，凡內帑奇貨，悉輦歸私邸，仍縱軍大掠，兩日方止。
units.en: The next day he moved the emperor to the Kaifeng prefectural quarters, had all the rare goods of the inner treasury carted to his private residence, and let his troops plunder freely for two days before it stopped.
units.literal: The next day he moved the emperor to the quarters of the Kaifeng prefecture; all the rare goods of the inner treasury he had carted to his private residence, and he still let the army plunder on a great scale for two days before it stopped.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·李處耘傳》云：居京師，遇張彥澤之暴，處耘善射，獨當裏門，殺數十人，里中賴之。）〉
units.en: (Eastern Capital Miscellany, biography of Li Chuyun: While in the capital he met Zhang Yanze's rampage. Chuyun was skilled at archery, held the lane gate alone, killed dozens of men, and the neighborhood was saved by him.)〉
units.literal: (Eastern Capital Miscellany, biography of Li Chuyun: While living in the capital he met Zhang Yanze's violence; Chuyun was skilled at archery, alone held the lane gate, killed several tens of men, and the neighborhood relied on him.)〉

units.zh: 時桑維翰為開封尹，彥澤召至麾下，待之不以禮。
units.en: Sang Weihan was then prefect of Kaifeng. Yanze summoned him to his camp and treated him without courtesy.
units.literal: At that time Sang Weihan was prefect of Kaifeng; Yanze summoned him under his command and did not treat him with courtesy.

units.zh: 維翰責曰：「去年拔公於罪人之中，復領大鎮，授以兵權，何負恩一至此耶？」
units.en: Weihan reproached him: "Last year I pulled you out of disgrace, restored you to a great command, and gave you military authority—how can your ingratitude have come to this?"
units.literal: Weihan reproached him, saying, "Last year I pulled you out from among criminals, restored you to a great commandery, and gave you military authority—how can your ingratitude have reached this point?"

units.zh: 彥澤無以對。
units.en: Yanze had no reply.
units.literal: Yanze had nothing to say in reply.

units.zh: 是夜殺維翰，盡取其家財。
units.en: That night he killed Weihan and seized all his household wealth.
units.literal: That night he killed Weihan and took all his household wealth.

units.zh: 彥澤自謂有功於契丹，晝夜以酒樂自娛。
units.en: Yanze believed he had rendered great service to the Khitan and spent day and night in wine and revelry.
units.literal: Yanze considered himself meritorious toward the Khitan and day and night amused himself with wine and music.

units.zh: 當在京巡檢之時，出入騎從常數百人，旗幟之上題曰「赤心為主」，觀者無不竊笑。
units.en: While serving as capital patrol inspector, he went about with several hundred horsemen in attendance. His banners bore the words "Loyal heart for the ruler," and every onlooker snickered behind his sleeve.
units.literal: While serving as capital patrol inspector, he went out and in with several hundred horsemen as escort; on his banners was written "Loyal heart for the ruler," and none of the onlookers failed to laugh behind their sleeves.

units.zh: 又所居第，財貨山積。
units.en: His residence, too, was heaped with wealth like a mountain.
units.literal: Moreover, in the residence where he lived, wealth was piled like mountains.

units.zh: 楚國夫人丁氏，即少帝弟曹州節度使延煦之母也，有容色，彥澤使人取之，太后遲回未與，彥澤立遣人載之而去，其負國欺君也如是。
units.en: Lady Ding of Chu, mother of Shaodi's brother Yanxu, military governor of Caozhou, was a woman of beauty. Yanze sent men to take her. The empress dowager hesitated to hand her over, so Yanze immediately had her carried off. Such was his treason against the state and deceit toward his sovereign.
units.literal: Lady Ding of Chu, mother of Emperor Shaodi's brother Yanxu, military governor of Caozhou, was beautiful in appearance; Yanze sent men to take her; the empress dowager hesitated and did not give her up; Yanze immediately sent men to carry her off—such was his betrayal of the state and deception of his lord.

units.zh: 數日之內，恣行殺害，或軍士擒獲罪人至前，彥澤不問所犯，但瞋目出一手豎三指而已，軍士承其意，即出外斷其腰領焉。
units.en: Within days he killed at will. When soldiers brought a prisoner before him, Yanze never asked the crime but only glared and held up three fingers on one hand. The soldiers understood and went out to cut the man in two at the waist.
units.literal: Within a few days he killed at will; sometimes when soldiers brought a captured criminal before him, Yanze did not ask the offense but only glared and held up one hand with three fingers raised; the soldiers understood his intent and at once went out and severed the victim at the waist.

units.zh: 彥澤與偽閣門使高勛不協，因乘醉至其門，害其仲父、季弟，暴屍於門外。
units.en: Yanze was at odds with the false gate commissioner Gao Xun. Drunk, he came to Xun's gate, killed his second uncle and younger brother, and left their corpses exposed outside.
units.literal: Yanze was at odds with the false gate commissioner Gao Xun; taking advantage of drunkenness he came to his gate, killed his second uncle and younger brother, and exposed their corpses outside the gate.

units.zh: 及契丹帳泊於北郊，勛往訴其冤，時契丹主已怒彥澤剽掠京城，遂令鎖之。
units.en: When the Khitan camp was pitched in the northern suburbs, Xun went to plead his wrong. The Khitan ruler was already enraged at Yanze's plunder of the capital and ordered him shackled.
units.literal: When the Khitan encampment was pitched in the northern suburbs, Xun went to plead his wrong; by then the Khitan ruler was already angry at Yanze's plunder of the capital and ordered him shackled.

units.zh: 仍以彥澤罪惡宣示百官及京城士庶，且云：「彥澤之罪，合誅與否？」
units.en: He also displayed Yanze's crimes before officials and people of the capital, asking, "Do Yanze's crimes merit execution?"
units.literal: He also displayed Yanze's crimes before the hundred officials and the people of the capital, saying, "Are Yanze's crimes fit for execution or not?"

units.zh: 百官連狀具言罪在不赦，市肆百姓亦爭投狀，疏彥澤之罪。
units.en: Officials submitted linked petitions declaring his crimes unpardonable, and townspeople in the markets vied to submit petitions listing his crimes.
units.literal: The hundred officials submitted linked petitions stating his crimes were unpardonable; commoners in the markets also vied to submit petitions detailing Yanze's crimes.

units.zh: 戎王知其眾怒，遂令棄市，仍令高勛監決，斷腕出鎖，然後刑之。
units.en: Seeing the people's wrath, the Khitan ruler ordered him executed in the marketplace and had Gao Xun supervise. His wrist was cut to remove the shackles, and only then was he executed.
units.literal: The barbarian king, knowing the people's wrath, then ordered him executed in the marketplace and still had Gao Xun supervise the execution; his wrist was cut to remove the shackles, and only then was he put to death.

units.zh: 勛使人剖其心以祭死者，市人爭其肉而食之。
units.en: Xun had his heart cut out to sacrifice to the dead. People in the market fought over his flesh and ate it.
units.literal: Xun had men cut open his heart to sacrifice to the dead; people in the market fought over his flesh and ate it.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：李濤常憤張彥澤殺邠州幕吏張式而取其妻，濤率同列上疏，請誅彥澤以謝西土，高祖方姑息武夫，竟不從。
units.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Li Tao often resented that Zhang Yanze had killed the Binzhou staff officer Zhang Shi and taken his wife. Tao led his colleagues in memorializing for Yanze's execution to appease the western command, but Gaozu was indulging military men and would not comply.)
units.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Li Tao often resented that Zhang Yanze killed the Binzhou staff officer Zhang Shi and took his wife; Tao led his colleagues in a memorial requesting Yanze be executed to appease the western lands; Emperor Gaozu was then indulging military men and ultimately did not comply.)

units.zh: 未幾，契丹南侵，至中渡橋，彥澤首降。
units.en: Before long the Khitan invaded south as far as Zhongdu Bridge, and Yanze was the first to surrender.
units.literal: Before long the Khitan invaded south, reaching Zhongdu Bridge; Yanze was the first to surrender.

units.zh: 戎王喜，命以本軍統蕃部控弦之士，先入京師。
units.en: The Khitan ruler was pleased and ordered him to lead the tribal archers of his own army into the capital first.
units.literal: The barbarian king was pleased and ordered him to lead the archers of the tribal forces of his own army to enter the capital first.

units.zh: 彥澤自以功不世出，乃挾宿憾殺開封尹桑維翰。
units.en: Yanze believed his merit unmatched and, nursing an old grudge, killed Sang Weihan, prefect of Kaifeng.
units.literal: Yanze considered his merit unmatched in the age and, nursing an old grudge, killed Sang Weihan, prefect of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 濤聞之，謂親知曰：「吾曾上疏請誅彥澤，今國家失守，彥澤所為如此，吾之首領容可保乎！
units.en: When Tao heard this he told his intimates: "I once memorialized asking that Yanze be executed. Now the state has fallen and Yanze acts like this—can my head still be safe?
units.literal: When Tao heard this he told his intimates, saying, "I once memorialized requesting Yanze be executed; now the state has lost its grip and Yanze acts like this—can my head still be kept safe?

units.zh: 然無可奈何，誰能伏藏溝瀆而取辱耶！」
units.en: Yet nothing could be done. Who would hide in a ditch and invite disgrace?"
units.literal: Yet there was nothing to be done—who can hide in ditches and invite disgrace!"

units.zh: 於是自寫門狀，求見彥澤。
units.en: He then wrote his own gate petition and asked to see Yanze.
units.literal: He then wrote his own gate petition himself and requested an audience with Yanze.

units.zh: 其狀云：「上疏請殺太尉人李濤，謹隨狀納命。」
units.en: The petition read: "Li Tao, who memorialized requesting the Grand Preceptor's execution, hereby submits his life with this petition."
units.literal: The petition read: "Li Tao, who memorialized requesting the Grand Preceptor be killed, respectfully submits his life with this petition."

units.zh: 彥澤覽之，欣然降階迎之。
units.en: Yanze read it and gladly came down the steps to welcome him.
units.literal: When Yanze read it he gladly came down the steps to welcome him.

units.zh: 然濤猶未安，復曰：「太尉果然相恕乎？」
units.en: Yet Tao was still uneasy and asked again, "Has the Grand Preceptor truly forgiven me?"
units.literal: Yet Tao was still uneasy and again said, "Has the Grand Preceptor truly forgiven me?"

units.zh: 彥澤曰：「覽公門狀，見『納命』二字，使人怒氣頓息，又何憂哉！」
units.en: Yanze said, "Reading your gate petition and seeing the words 'submit life,' my anger vanished at once—what is there to worry about?"
units.literal: Yanze said, "Reading your gate petition and seeing the two characters 'submit life,' one's anger suddenly subsides—what is there to worry about!"

units.zh: 濤素滑稽，知其必免，又戲為伶人詞曰：「太尉既相恕，何不將壓驚絹來。」
units.en: Tao was naturally witty. Knowing he would escape, he jested in an actor's lines: "Since the Grand Preceptor has forgiven me, why not bring the silk to calm my fright?"
units.literal: Tao had always been witty; knowing he would surely escape, he again jested in the words of an actor, saying, "Since the Grand Preceptor has forgiven me, why not bring the silk to calm my fright?"

units.zh: 彥澤大笑，卒善待之。）〉
units.en: Yanze laughed loudly and in the end treated him well.)〉
units.literal: Yanze laughed loudly and in the end treated him well.)〉

units.zh: 趙德鈞，本名行實，幽州人也。
units.en: Zhao Dejun, whose original name was Xingshi, was a native of Youzhou.
units.literal: Zhao Dejun, original name Xingshi, was a man of Youzhou.

units.zh: 少以騎射事滄州連帥劉守文，守文為弟守光所害，遂事守光，署為幽州軍校。
units.en: In youth he served the Cangzhou military governor Liu Shouwen as a horseman and archer. When Shouwen was killed by his younger brother Shouguang, he entered Shouguang's service and was made an army officer at Youzhou.
units.literal: In youth he served the Cangzhou military governor Liu Shouwen with riding and archery; Shouwen was killed by his younger brother Shouguang, whereupon he served Shouguang and was appointed a Youzhou army officer.

units.zh: 及唐莊宗伐幽州，德鈞知其必敗，乃遁歸莊宗。
units.en: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong attacked Youzhou, Dejun knew Shouguang would fail and fled to Zhuangzong's side.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang attacked Youzhou, Dejun knew he would certainly be defeated and therefore fled back to Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 莊宗善待之，賜姓，名曰紹斌，累歷郡守，從平梁，遷滄州節度使。
units.en: Zhuangzong treated him well, bestowed the imperial surname, and named him Shaobin. He served in successive prefectures, followed the pacification of Liang, and was made military governor of Cangzhou.
units.literal: Zhuangzong treated him well, bestowed a surname, and named him Shaobin; he successively held prefectures, followed in pacifying Liang, and was transferred to military governor of Cangzhou.

units.zh: 同光三年，移鎮幽州。
units.en: In the third Tongguang year he was transferred to command Youzhou.
units.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was transferred to command Youzhou.

units.zh: 明宗即位，遂歸本姓，始改名德鈞。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne he resumed his original surname and first took the name Dejun.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne he returned to his original surname and first changed his name to Dejun.

units.zh: 其子延壽尚明宗女興平公主，故德鈞尤承倚重。
units.en: His son Yanshou married Mingzong's daughter Princess Xingping, so Dejun enjoyed exceptional favor and trust.
units.literal: His son Yanshou married Emperor Mingzong's daughter Princess Xingping; therefore Dejun was especially favored and relied upon.

units.zh: 天成中，定州王都反，契丹遣惕隱領精騎五千來援都，至唐河，為招討使王晏球所敗。
units.en: During the Tiancheng era Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled. The Khitan sent a tiyin with five thousand elite horsemen to aid him, but at Tanghe they were defeated by Pacification Commissioner Wang Yanqiu.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled; the Khitan sent a tiyin leading five thousand elite horsemen to aid Du; reaching Tanghe, they were defeated by the pacification commissioner Wang Yanqiu.

units.zh: 會霖雨相繼，所在泥淖，敗兵北走，人馬饑疲，德鈞於要路邀之，盡獲餘眾，擒特哩袞已下首領數十人，獻於京師。
units.en: Rain fell in succession and the roads turned to mire. The defeated army fled north, men and horses starving and spent. Dejun intercepted them at a strategic pass, captured all who remained, and seized dozens of leaders including Teligun, whom he sent to the capital.
units.literal: It happened that rain fell in succession and everywhere was mire; the defeated army fled north, men and horses hungry and exhausted; Dejun intercepted them at a strategic pass, captured all the remaining troops, seized several tens of leaders including Teligun and below, and presented them at the capital.

units.zh: 明年，王都平，加兼侍中，頃之，加東北面招討使。
units.en: The next year Wang Du was pacified. Dejun was made Vice Grand Counselor and soon after Northeast Frontier Pacification Commissioner.
units.literal: The next year Wang Du was pacified; he was additionally made Vice Grand Counselor, and soon after made Northeast Frontier Pacification Commissioner.

units.zh: 德鈞奏發河北數鎮丁夫，開王馬口至遊口，以通水運凡二百里。
units.en: Dejun memorialized to mobilize laborers from several Hebei commands and open a channel from Wangmakou to Youkou, linking water transport for two hundred li.
units.literal: Dejun memorialized to mobilize laborers from several Hebei commands, open a channel from Wangmakou to Youkou, and connect water transport for a total of two hundred li.

units.zh: 又於閻溝築壘，以戍兵守之，因名良鄉縣，以備鈔寇。
units.en: He also built a fort at Yancou and garrisoned it, naming the place Liangxiang County to guard against raiders.
units.literal: He also built a fort at Yancou, garrisoned it with troops, and thereby named Liangxiang County to guard against raiding enemies.

units.zh: 又於幽州東築三河城，北接薊州，頗為形勝之要，部民由是稍得樵牧。
units.en: He also built Sanhe Fort east of Youzhou, linking north to Jizhou at a point of great strategic value, so that the people of his command could again gather fuelwood and pasture their herds.
units.literal: He also built Sanhe Fort east of Youzhou, connecting north to Jizhou—a place of considerable strategic advantage—so that the people of his command could gradually gather fuel and pasture their herds.

units.zh: 德鈞鎮幽州凡十餘年，甚有善政，累官至檢校太師、兼中書令，封北平王。
units.en: Dejun governed Youzhou for more than ten years with notable good administration, rose to Honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Grand Counselor, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping.
units.literal: Dejun governed Youzhou for more than ten years in all and had very good administration; he rose in rank to Honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Grand Counselor and was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping.

units.zh: 〈（《遼史》：天贊六年，遣人以詔賜盧龍軍節度使趙德鈞。
units.en: (Liao History: In the sixth Tianzan year an envoy was sent with an edict for Zhao Dejun, military governor of the Lulong army.)
units.literal: (Liao History: In the sixth year of Tianzan an envoy was sent with an edict bestowed on Zhao Dejun, military governor of the Lulong army.)

units.zh: 七年，趙德鈞遣人進時果。
units.en: In the seventh year Zhao Dejun sent tribute of seasonal fruits.
units.literal: In the seventh year Zhao Dejun sent men presenting seasonal fruits.

units.zh: 蓋德鈞久在邊境，嘗與契丹通好也。）〉
units.en: Dejun had long been on the frontier and had once maintained friendly relations with the Khitan.)〉
units.literal: For Dejun had long been on the frontier and had once maintained friendly relations with the Khitan.)〉

units.zh: 清泰三年夏，晉高祖起義於晉陽。
units.en: In the summer of the third Qingtai year, Jin Emperor Gaozu rose in revolt at Jinyang.
units.literal: In the summer of the third year of Qingtai, Emperor Gaozu of Jin rose in revolt at Jinyang.

units.zh: 九月，契丹敗張敬達之軍於太原城下，唐末帝詔德鈞以本軍由飛狐路出賊後邀之。
units.en: In the ninth month the Khitan defeated Zhang Jingda's army below Taiyuan. The last Tang emperor ordered Dejun to lead his army by the Feihu route and strike the rebels from behind.
units.literal: In the ninth month the Khitan defeated Zhang Jingda's army below Taiyuan city; the last Tang emperor ordered Dejun to lead his own army by the Feihu route to strike the rebels from behind and intercept them.

units.zh: 時德鈞子延壽為樞密使，唐末帝命帥軍屯上黨，德鈞乃以所部銀鞍契丹直三千騎至鎮州，率節度使華溫琪同赴征行，自吳兒峪路趨昭義，與延壽會於西唐店。
units.en: Dejun's son Yanshou was then Commissioner of Military Affairs. The last Tang emperor ordered him to garrison Shangdang. Dejun led three thousand Silver Saddle Khitan guards to Zhenzhou, took Military Governor Hua Wenqi with him on campaign, advanced by the Wu'eryu route toward Zhaoyi, and joined Yanshou at Xitangdian.
units.literal: At that time Dejun's son Yanshou was Commissioner of Military Affairs; the last Tang emperor ordered him to command troops garrisoned at Shangdang; Dejun then led three thousand Silver Saddle Khitan guards of his command to Zhenzhou, took the military governor Hua Wenqi with him on the campaign, advanced by the Wu'eryu route toward Zhaoyi, and joined Yanshou at Xitangdian.

units.zh: 十一月，以德鈞為諸道行營都統，以延壽為太原南面招討使，遣端明殿學士呂琦賫賜官告，兼令犒軍。
units.en: In the eleventh month Dejun was made overall commander of all campaign armies and Yanshou Southern Pacification Commissioner against Taiyuan. Hanlin academician Lü Qi was sent with commissions and orders to reward the troops.
units.literal: In the eleventh month Dejun was made overall commander of the campaign armies of all circuits and Yanshou made Southern Pacification Commissioner against Taiyuan; the Hanlin academician Lü Qi was sent bearing bestowed commissions and also ordered to reward the troops.

units.zh: 琦從容言天子委任之意，德鈞曰：「既以兵相委，焉敢惜死。」
units.en: Qi calmly conveyed the Son of Heaven's trust. Dejun said, "Since troops have been entrusted to me, how dare I spare my life?"
units.literal: Qi calmly spoke of the Son of Heaven's intent in entrusting him; Dejun said, "Since troops have been entrusted to me, how dare I spare my life."

units.zh: 時範延光領兵二萬軍於遼州，德鈞欲並其軍，奏請與延光會合。
units.en: Fan Yanguang then commanded twenty thousand troops at Liaozhou. Dejun wished to absorb his force and memorialized to join with him.
units.literal: At that time Fan Yanguang commanded twenty thousand troops garrisoned at Liaozhou; Dejun wished to absorb his army and memorialized requesting to join with Yanguang.

units.zh: 唐末帝諭延光，疑其奸謀，不從。
units.en: The last Tang emperor instructed Yanguang, suspecting treachery, and Yanguang refused.
units.literal: The last Tang emperor instructed Yanguang, suspecting a treacherous plot, and he did not comply.

units.zh: 德鈞、延壽自潞州引軍至團柏谷，德鈞累奏乞授延壽鎮州節度，末帝不悅，謂左右曰：「趙德鈞父子堅要鎮州，茍能逐退蕃戎，要代予位，亦所甘心；
units.en: Dejun and Yanshou led their army from Luzhou to Tuanbai Valley. Dejun repeatedly memorialized asking that Yanshou be made military governor of Zhenzhou. The last emperor was displeased and told his attendants: "The Zhao Dejun father and son insist on Zhenzhou. If they can drive off the barbarians, I would gladly yield my throne to them;
units.literal: Dejun and Yanshou led their army from Luzhou to Tuanbai Valley; Dejun repeatedly memorialized begging that Yanshou be given the Zhenzhou command; the last emperor was displeased and told those around him, "Zhao Dejun father and son insist on Zhenzhou; if they can drive off the barbarians, even if they want to take my place in my stead, I would be content;

units.zh: 若玩寇要君，但恐犬兔俱斃。」
units.en: but if they toy with the enemy and coerce their sovereign, I fear both dog and hare will die together."
units.literal: but if they toy with the enemy and coerce their lord, I fear both dog and hare will perish together."

units.zh: 朝廷繼馳書詔，促令進軍，德鈞持疑不果，乃遣使於契丹，厚賫金幣，求立以為帝，仍許晉祖長鎮太原，契丹主不之許。
units.en: The court sent urgent edicts pressing them to advance, but Dejun hesitated and did not move. He then sent envoys to the Khitan with rich gifts of gold and coin, asking to be made emperor and promising that the Jin founder could long govern Taiyuan. The Khitan ruler refused.
units.literal: The court then sent urgent edicts by relay, pressing them to advance; Dejun hesitated and did not act; he then sent envoys to the Khitan with rich gifts of gold and coin, asking to be established as emperor and still promising that the Jin founder would long govern Taiyuan—the Khitan ruler did not grant it.

units.zh: 及楊光遠以晉安寨降於契丹，德鈞父子自團柏谷南走潞州，一行兵士，投戈棄甲，自相騰踐，死者萬計。
units.en: When Yang Guangyuan surrendered Jin'an Stockade to the Khitan, Dejun and his son fled south from Tuanbai Valley to Luzhou. The soldiers cast away weapons and armor, trampled one another in flight, and died by the tens of thousands.
units.literal: When Yang Guangyuan surrendered Jin'an Stockade to the Khitan, Dejun father and son fled south from Tuanbai Valley to Luzhou; the soldiers along the way cast away spears and armor, trampled one another, and died by the tens of thousands.

units.zh: 時德鈞有愛將時賽，率輕騎東還漁陽，其部曲尚千餘人，與散亡之卒俱集於潞州。
units.en: Dejun's favorite general Shi Sai led light cavalry east back to Yuyang with more than a thousand followers still under him. Together with scattered fugitives they all gathered at Luzhou.
units.literal: At that time Dejun had a favorite general Shi Sai, who led light cavalry east back to Yuyang; his followers still numbered more than a thousand, and together with scattered fugitive troops they all gathered at Luzhou.

units.zh: 是日，潞州節度使高行周亦自北還，及至府門，見德鈞父子在城上，行周謂曰：「某與大王鄉人，宜以忠言相告，城中無鬥粟可食，請大王速迎車駕，自圖安計，無取後悔焉。」
units.en: That day Military Governor Gao Xingzhou also returned from the north. At the prefectural gate he saw Dejun and his son on the wall and said: "Your Highness and I are townsmen, so I speak plainly: there is not a dou of grain left in the city. Welcome the imperial carriage at once, secure your own safety, and do not invite regret."
units.literal: That day the military governor of Luzhou Gao Xingzhou also returned from the north; when he reached the prefectural gate he saw Dejun father and son on the wall; Xingzhou said to them, "I and Your Highness are fellow townsmen and ought to speak loyal words: there is not a dou of grain to eat in the city—please Your Highness quickly welcome the imperial carriage, seek your own safety, and do not bring on regret."

units.zh: 德鈞遂與延壽出降契丹。
units.en: Dejun then went out with Yanshou and surrendered to the Khitan.
units.literal: Dejun then went out with Yanshou and surrendered to the Khitan.

units.zh: 高祖至，德鈞父子迎謁於馬前，高祖不禮之。
units.en: When Gaozu arrived, Dejun and his son met him before his horse, but Gaozu showed them no courtesy.
units.literal: When Gaozu arrived, Dejun father and son met and paid respects before his horse; Gaozu did not treat them courteously.

units.zh: 時契丹主問德鈞曰：「汝在幽州日，所置銀鞍契丹直何在？」
units.en: The Khitan ruler asked Dejun: "When you were in Youzhou, where are the Silver Saddle Khitan guards you raised?"
units.literal: At that time the Khitan ruler asked Dejun, saying, "When you were in Youzhou, where are the Silver Saddle Khitan guards you established?"

units.zh: 德鈞指示之，契丹盡殺於潞之西郊，遂鎖德鈞父子入蕃。
units.en: Dejun pointed them out. The Khitan killed them all in the western suburbs of Lu, then shackled Dejun and his son and took them into Khitan territory.
units.literal: Dejun pointed them out; the Khitan killed them all in the western suburbs of Lu and then shackled Dejun father and son and took them into the barbarian lands.

units.zh: 及見國母述律氏，盡以一行財寶及幽州田宅籍而獻之，國母謂之曰：「汝父子自覓天子何耶？」
units.en: When he met Empress Dowager Shulü, he presented all the wealth of his party and registered his Youzhou fields and houses as gifts. The empress dowager said to him: "Why did you father and son go seeking a Son of Heaven for yourselves?"
units.literal: When he met the empress dowager Shulü, he presented all the wealth of his party and registered his Youzhou fields and houses as gifts; the empress dowager said to him, "Why did you father and son go seeking a Son of Heaven for yourselves?"

units.zh: 德鈞俯首不能對。
units.en: Dejun bowed his head and could not answer.
units.literal: Dejun bowed his head and could not answer.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：太后問曰：「汝近者何為在太原？」
units.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: The empress dowager asked, "What were you doing recently at Taiyuan?"
units.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: The empress dowager asked, saying, "What were you doing recently at Taiyuan?"

units.zh: 德鈞曰：「奉唐主之命。」
units.en: Dejun said, "Following the Tang ruler's command."
units.literal: Dejun said, "Following the Tang ruler's command."

units.zh: 太后曰：「汝從吾兒求為天子，何妄語耶！」
units.en: The empress dowager said, "You asked my son to make you Son of Heaven—what nonsense is this?"
units.literal: The empress dowager said, "You asked my son to make you Son of Heaven—what false words are these!"

units.zh: 又自指其心曰：「此不可欺也。」
units.en: She pointed at her own heart and said, "This cannot be deceived."
units.literal: She also pointed at her own heart and said, "This cannot be deceived."

units.zh: 又曰：「吾兒將行，吾戒之云：『趙大王若引兵北向榆關，亟須引歸，太原不可救也。』
units.en: She also said, "When my son was about to march, I warned him: 'If King Zhao leads troops north toward Yuguan, recall him at once—Taiyuan cannot be saved.'
units.literal: She also said, "When my son was about to march, I warned him, saying, 'If King Zhao leads troops north toward Yuguan, he must be recalled at once—Taiyuan cannot be saved.'

units.zh: 汝欲為天子，何不先擊退吾兒，徐圖亦未晚。
units.en: If you wished to be Son of Heaven, why not first defeat my son? Plotting more slowly would not have been too late.
units.literal: If you wished to be Son of Heaven, why not first strike and drive off my son—plotting slowly would not have been too late.

units.zh: 汝為人臣，既負其主，不能擊敵，又欲乘亂邀利，所為如此，何面目復求生乎？」
units.en: You are a subject who betrayed your lord, could not strike the enemy, and still wished to profit from chaos. Acting like this, with what face can you seek to live?"
units.literal: You are a subject, yet you betrayed your lord, could not strike the enemy, and still wished to seize profit amid chaos—acting like this, with what face can you seek to live again?"

units.zh: 德鈞俯首不能對。）〉
units.en: Dejun bowed his head and could not answer.)〉
units.literal: Dejun bowed his head and could not answer.)〉

units.zh: 又問：「田宅何在？」
units.en: She asked again, "Where are the fields and houses?"
units.literal: She asked again, "Where are the fields and houses?"

units.zh: 曰：「俱在幽州。」
units.en: He said, "All are in Youzhou."
units.literal: He said, "All are in Youzhou."

units.zh: 國母曰：「屬我矣，又何獻也？」
units.en: The empress dowager said, "They already belong to me—why present them again?"
units.literal: The empress dowager said, "They already belong to me—why present them again?"

units.zh: 至天福二年夏，德鈞卒於契丹。
units.en: By the summer of the second Tianfu year, Dejun died in Khitan territory.
units.literal: By the summer of the second year of Tianfu, Dejun died among the Khitan.

units.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》：德鈞郁郁不多食，逾年而死。
units.en: (Khitan State Chronicle: Dejun grew depressed and ate little; after more than a year he died.)
units.literal: (Khitan State Chronicle: Dejun was depressed and ate little; after more than a year he died.)

units.zh: 德鈞既卒，國主釋延壽而用之。）〉
units.en: After Dejun died, the Khitan ruler released Yanshou and employed him.)〉
units.literal: After Dejun died, the state ruler released Yanshou and employed him.)〉

units.zh: 延壽，本姓劉氏。
units.en: Yanshou was originally surnamed Liu.
units.literal: Yanshou was originally surnamed Liu.

units.zh: 父曰邧，常山人也，嘗任蓚令。
units.en: His father was named Kuang, a man of Changshan who had once served as magistrate of Tiao.
units.literal: His father was named Kuang, a man of Changshan who had once served as magistrate of Tiao.

units.zh: 梁開平初，滄州節度使劉守文陷其邑，時德鈞為偏將，獲延壽並其母種氏，遂養之為子。
units.en: Early in Liang's Kaiping era the Cangzhou military governor Liu Shouwen overran his county. Dejun was then a deputy general, captured Yanshou together with his mother Lady Zhong, and adopted him as his son.
units.literal: Early in Liang's Kaiping era the Cangzhou military governor Liu Shouwen overran his county. Dejun was then a deputy general, captured Yanshou together with his mother Lady Zhong, and adopted him as son.

units.zh: 延壽姿貌妍柔，稍涉書史，尤好賓客，亦能為詩。
units.en: Yanshou had a graceful and delicate appearance, had some knowledge of books and history, especially loved entertaining guests, and could also compose poetry.
units.literal: Yanshou had a graceful and delicate appearance, had some knowledge of books and history, especially loved entertaining guests, and could also compose poetry.

units.zh: （《太平廣記》引《趙延壽傳》云：延壽幼習武略，即戎之暇，時復以篇什為意，嘗在北庭賦詩曰：「占得高原肥草地，夜深生火折林梢。」
units.en: (Extensive Records of the Taiping Era, citing the Biography of Zhao Yanshou, says: Yanshou in youth studied military strategy, and in intervals from campaigning would turn to verse. Once at Beiting he composed a poem saying, "Choosing a fat meadow on the high plain, deep in the night I kindle fire and break off treetops."
units.literal: (Extensive Records of the Taiping Era, citing the Biography of Zhao Yanshou, says: Yanshou in youth studied military strategy, and in intervals from campaigning would turn to verse. Once at Beiting he composed a poem saying, "Choosing a fat meadow on the high plain, deep in the night I kindle fire and break off treetops."

units.zh: 南人聞者傳之。）
units.en: Southerners who heard it spread it about.)
units.literal: Southerners who heard it spread it about.)

units.zh: 及長，尚明宗女興平公主。
units.en: When he came of age he married Mingzong's daughter Princess Xingping.
units.literal: When he came of age he married Mingzong's daughter Princess Xingping.

units.zh: 初為汴州司馬，明宗即位，授汝州刺史，歷河陽、宋州節度使，入為上將軍，充宣徽使，遷樞密使，兼鎮徐州。
units.en: At first he was vice prefect of Bianzhou. When Mingzong took the throne he was made prefect of Ruzhou, held the military governorships of Heyang and Songzhou in succession, entered court as Grand General, served as Palace Commissioner, was transferred to Commissioner of Military Affairs, and concurrently commanded Xuzhou.
units.literal: At first he was vice prefect of Bianzhou. When Mingzong took the throne he was made prefect of Ruzhou, held the military governorships of Heyang and Songzhou in succession, entered court as Grand General, served as Palace Commissioner, was transferred to Commissioner of Military Affairs, and concurrently commanded Xuzhou.

units.zh: 及高祖起義於晉陽，唐末帝幸懷州，委延壽北伐。
units.en: When Gaozu raised righteous arms at Jinyang, Tang's last emperor went to Huaizhou and entrusted Yanshou with the northern campaign.
units.literal: When Gaozu raised righteous arms at Jinyang, Tang's last emperor went to Huaizhou and entrusted Yanshou with the northern campaign.

units.zh: 後高祖至潞州，延壽與父德鈞俱陷北庭。
units.en: Later when Gaozu reached Luzhou, Yanshou and his father Dejun both fell into Khitan hands.
units.literal: Later when Gaozu reached Luzhou, Yanshou and his father Dejun both fell into Khitan hands.

units.zh: 未幾，契丹主以延壽為幽州節度使，封燕王，尋為樞密使兼政事令。
units.en: Before long the Khitan ruler made Yanshou military governor of Youzhou, enfeoffed him as Prince of Yan, and soon made him Commissioner of Military Affairs and concurrently Director of State Affairs.
units.literal: Before long the Khitan ruler made Yanshou military governor of Youzhou, enfeoffed him as Prince of Yan, and soon made him Commissioner of Military Affairs and concurrently Director of State Affairs.

units.zh: 天福末，契丹與少帝絕好，契丹主委延壽以圖南之事，許以中原帝之。
units.en: At the end of the Tianfu era the Khitan broke with Emperor Shaodi. The Khitan ruler entrusted Yanshou with the southern campaign and promised him the throne of the Central Plains.
units.literal: At the end of Tianfu the Khitan broke relations with Emperor Shaodi; the Khitan ruler entrusted Yanshou with the plan to march south and promised him the throne of the Central Plains.

units.zh: 延壽乃導誘蕃戎，蠶食河朔。
units.en: Yanshou then guided the barbarian forces, nibbling away at the lands north of the Yellow River.
units.literal: Yanshou then guided and enticed the barbarian forces, nibbling away at the lands north of the Yellow River.

units.zh: 晉軍既降於中渡，戎主命延壽就寨安撫諸寫，仍賜龍鳳褚袍，使衣之而往。
units.en: After the Jin army surrendered at Zhongdu, the Khitan ruler ordered Yanshou to the camps to comfort the various units, bestowed a dragon-phoenix crimson robe, and had him wear it when he went.
units.literal: After the Jin army surrendered at Zhongdu, the barbarian ruler ordered Yanshou to go to the camps and comfort the various units; he also bestowed a dragon-phoenix crimson robe and had him wear it when he went.

units.zh: 謂之曰：「漢兒兵士，皆爾有之，爾宜親自慰撫。」
units.en: He told him, "The Han soldiers are all yours now. Comfort and reassure them in person."
units.literal: He told him, "The Han soldiers are all yours; you ought to comfort and reassure them in person."

units.zh: 延壽至營，杜重威、李守貞已下皆迎謁於馬前。
units.en: When Yanshou reached the camp, Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, and the rest all met him before his horse.
units.literal: When Yanshou reached the camp, Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, and those below all met and paid respects before his horse.

units.zh: 及契丹入汴，時降軍數萬，皆野次於陳橋，契丹主慮有變，欲盡殺之。
units.en: When the Khitan entered Bian, tens of thousands of surrendered troops were encamped in the open at Chenqiao. The Khitan ruler feared trouble and wished to kill them all.
units.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, there were then several tens of thousands of surrendered troops all encamped in the open at Chenqiao; the Khitan ruler feared there might be trouble and wished to kill them all.

units.zh: 延壽聞之，遽請見戎王，曰：「臣伏見今日已前，皇帝百戰千征，始收得晉國，不知皇帝自要治之乎？
units.en: When Yanshou heard this he hurried to see the Khitan ruler and said: "Your servant observes that until today Your Majesty fought battle after battle before finally taking the Jin state. Does Your Majesty mean to rule it yourself?
units.literal: When Yanshou heard this he hurried to request an audience with the barbarian king and said, "Your servant humbly observes that up to today the emperor fought a hundred battles and a thousand campaigns before finally taking the Jin state—does the emperor mean to rule it himself?

units.zh: 為他人取之乎？」
units.en: Or have it taken for someone else?"
units.literal: Or have it taken for someone else?"

units.zh: 契丹主變色曰：「爾何言之過也！
units.en: The Khitan ruler's face changed and he said, "How excessive are your words!
units.literal: The Khitan ruler changed color and said, "How excessive are your words!

units.zh: 朕以晉人負義，舉國南征，五年相殺，方得中原，豈不自要為主，而為他人耶？
units.en: Because the Jin betrayed their pledges, I mobilized the whole state in a southern campaign. For five years we fought before gaining the Central Plains. Would I not rule it myself rather than hand it to another?
units.literal: I, because the Jin people betrayed faith, mobilized the whole state in a southern campaign; for five years we killed one another before finally gaining the Central Plains—would I not want to be master myself rather than for another?

units.zh: 卿有何說，速奏朕來！」
units.en: What have you to say? Speak quickly!"
units.literal: What have you to say—report quickly to me!"
