units.zh: 延壽曰：「皇帝嘗知吳、蜀與晉朝相殺否？」
units.en: Yanshou said, "Does Your Majesty know whether Wu and Shu fight the Jin court?"
units.literal: Yanshou said, "Has the emperor ever known whether Wu and Shu fight the Jin court?"

units.en: He said, "I know."
units.literal: He said, "I know."

units.zh: 延壽曰：「今中原南自安、申，西及秦、鳳，沿邊數千里，並是兩界守戍之所。
units.en: Yanshou said, "From An and Shen in the south to Qin and Feng in the west, the Central Plains frontier runs thousands of li, all of it garrisoned by both realms.
units.literal: Yanshou said, "Now the Central Plains from An and Shen in the south to Qin and Feng in the west—for several thousand li along the border—all are places where the two realms maintain garrisons.

units.zh: 將來皇帝歸國時，又漸及炎蒸，若吳、蜀二寇交侵中國，未知許大世界，教甚兵馬禦捍？
units.en: When Your Majesty returns home, the season will turn hot and steamy again. If Wu and Shu attack China together, who knows how vast the realm is—with what troops will you defend it?
units.literal: When the emperor returns to his state in the future, it will again gradually reach the season of heat and steam; if the two foes Wu and Shu attack China together, who knows how vast a realm it is—with what troops and horses will you defend it?

units.zh: 茍失堤防，豈非為他人取也。」
units.en: If the defenses fail, will it not be taken by others?"
units.literal: If the dikes and defenses are lost, will it not be taken for someone else?"

units.zh: 戎王曰：「我弗知也，為之奈何？」
units.en: The Khitan ruler said, "I do not know—what is to be done?"
units.literal: The barbarian king said, "I do not know—what is to be done?"

units.zh: 延壽曰：「臣知上國之兵，當炎暑之時，沿吳、蜀之境，難為用也。
units.en: Yanshou said, "Your Majesty's troops are hard to use in summer heat along the Wu and Shu frontiers.
units.literal: Yanshou said, "Your servant knows that the troops of the superior state, in the season of heat and summer, along the borders of Wu and Shu, are hard to employ.

units.zh: 未若以陳橋所聚降軍團並，別作軍額，以備邊防。」
units.en: Better to group the surrendered troops at Chenqiao into regiments under a separate army designation and use them to guard the frontier."
units.literal: It would be better to group the surrendered troops gathered at Chenqiao into regiments, establish a separate army designation, and use them to guard the frontier."

units.zh: 戎王曰：「我念在壺關、陽城時，亦曾言議，未獲區分，致五年相殺，此時入手，如何更不翦除？」
units.en: The Khitan ruler said, "I recall that at Huguan and Yangcheng we discussed this and failed to settle it, which led to five years of slaughter. Now that they are in hand, how can we not wipe them out?"
units.literal: The barbarian king said, "I recall that at Huguan and Yangcheng we also once discussed this and did not get it sorted out, which led to five years of mutual slaughter—now that they are in hand, how can we not exterminate them?"

units.zh: 延壽曰：「晉軍見在之數，如今還似從前盡在河南，誠為不可。
units.en: Yanshou said, "The Jin troops now here—if they are again all kept south of the river as before, that truly will not do.
units.literal: Yanshou said, "The Jin troops now present in number—if today they are again all south of the river as before, that truly cannot be allowed.

units.zh: 臣請遷其軍，並其家口於鎮、定、雲、朔間以處之，每歲差伊分番，於河外沿邊防戍，上策也。」
units.en: I ask that their army and families be moved to Zhen, Ding, Yun, and Shuo, and that they rotate in annual shifts to guard the frontier beyond the river. That is the best plan."
units.literal: Your servant requests that their army be moved, together with their households, to be settled among Zhen, Ding, Yun, and Shuo; each year detach them in rotating shifts to guard the frontier along the river's outer bank—the best plan."

units.zh: 戎王忻然曰：「一取大王商量。」
units.en: The Khitan ruler said gladly, "I leave it all to the King's counsel."
units.literal: The barbarian king said gladly, "I take it all for discussion with the King."

units.zh: 由是陳橋之眾獲免長平之禍焉。
units.en: Thus the troops at Chenqiao escaped the massacre of Changping.
units.literal: Thus the masses at Chenqiao escaped the calamity of Changping.

units.zh: 延壽在汴久之，知契丹主無踐言之意，乃遣李崧達語契丹主，求立為皇太子，崧不得已言之。
units.en: Yanshou had long been at Bian and knew the Khitan ruler would not keep his word. He sent Li Song to ask to be made crown prince. Song had no choice but to relay the request.
units.literal: Yanshou had long been at Bian and knew the Khitan ruler had no intent to keep his word; he then sent Li Song to convey words to the Khitan ruler requesting to be established as crown prince; Song had no choice but to speak of it.

units.zh: 契丹主曰：「我於燕王，無所愛惜，但我皮肉堪與燕王使用，亦可割也，何況他事！
units.en: The Khitan ruler said, "Toward the Prince of Yan I spare nothing. Even my own flesh, if the Prince of Yan can use it, may be cut away—how much more other matters!
units.literal: The Khitan ruler said, "Toward the Prince of Yan I spare nothing, but even my flesh and skin, if fit for the Prince of Yan's use, may be cut away—how much more other matters!

units.zh: 我聞皇太子，天子之子合作，燕王豈得為之也！」
units.en: I have heard that crown prince is a title for the Son of Heaven's own son. How can the Prince of Yan hold it?"
units.literal: I have heard that crown prince is a title for the Son of Heaven's own son—how can the Prince of Yan hold it!"

units.zh: 因命與燕王加恩。
units.en: He then ordered additional honors for the Prince of Yan.
units.literal: He then ordered additional favor be shown the Prince of Yan.

units.zh: 時北來翰林學士承旨張礪，擬延壽為中京留守、大丞相、錄尚書事、都督中外諸軍事，樞密使、燕王如故。
units.en: The Hanlin academician and chief drafter Zhang Li, who had come from the north, drafted an appointment for Yanshou as Middle Capital regent, Grand Chancellor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Commander of All Military Affairs, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Prince of Yan as before.
units.literal: At that time the Hanlin academician and chief drafter Zhang Li, who had come from the north, drafted Yanshou as Middle Capital regent, Grand Chancellor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Commander of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Prince of Yan as before.

units.zh: 契丹主覽狀，索筆圍卻「錄尚書事、都督中外諸軍事」之字，乃付翰林院草制焉。
units.en: The Khitan ruler reviewed the draft, circled out "Recorder of the Masters of Writing" and "Commander of All Military Affairs," and handed it to the Hanlin Academy to draft the edict.
units.literal: The Khitan ruler reviewed the draft, took a brush and circled out the characters for "Recorder of the Masters of Writing" and "Commander of All Military Affairs," and then handed it to the Hanlin Academy to draft the edict.

units.zh: 又以其子匡贊為河中節度使。
units.en: He also made his son Kuangzan military governor of Hezhong.
units.literal: He also made his son Kuangzan military governor of Hezhong.

units.zh: 延壽在汴州，復娶明宗小女為繼室。
units.en: At Bianzhou, Yanshou took another younger daughter of Mingzong as his successor wife.
units.literal: While at Bianzhou, Yanshou again married a younger daughter of Emperor Mingzong as his successor wife.

units.zh: 先是，延州節度使周密為其子廣娶焉，已納財畢，親迎有日矣，至是延壽奪取之。
units.en: Earlier Military Governor Zhou Mi of Yanzhou had arranged for his son Guang to marry her. The bride-price had been paid and the wedding day set, but Yanshou seized her for himself.
units.literal: Earlier the military governor of Yanzhou Zhou Mi had arranged for his son Guang to marry her; the bride-price had been paid and the wedding day set, but at this point Yanshou seized her for himself.

units.zh: 契丹主自汴回至邢州，命升延壽坐在契丹左右相之上。
units.en: When the Khitan ruler returned from Bian to Xingzhou, he seated Yanshou above the Khitan left and right chancellors.
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler returned from Bian to Xingzhou, he ordered Yanshou raised to a seat above the Khitan left and right chancellors.

units.zh: 契丹主死，延壽下教於諸道，稱權知南朝軍國事。
units.en: When the Khitan ruler died, Yanshou issued orders to the circuits styling himself provisional controller of the southern dynasty's military and civil affairs.
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler died, Yanshou issued instructions to the various circuits, styling himself provisional controller of the southern dynasty's military and state affairs.

units.zh: 是歲六月一日，為永康王烏裕所鎖，籍其家財，分給諸部。
units.en: On the first day of the sixth month that year he was shackled by Prince Yongkang Wuyu. His household wealth was inventoried and distributed among the tribes.
units.literal: On the first day of the sixth month of that year he was shackled by Prince Yongkang Wuyu; his household wealth was registered and distributed among the various tribes.

units.zh: 尋以延壽入國，竟卒於契丹。
units.en: Soon after Yanshou entered Khitan territory, he died there.
units.literal: Soon after, as Yanshou entered the Khitan state, he ultimately died among the Khitan.

units.zh: 匡贊歷漢、周兩朝，累授節鎮及統軍使。
units.en: Kuangzan served through the Han and Zhou dynasties and was repeatedly appointed to military commands and army leadership.
units.literal: Kuangzan served through the Han and Zhou dynasties and was repeatedly appointed to military governorships and army command.

units.zh: 仕皇朝，歷廬、延、邠、鄜等四鎮焉。
units.en: Under the imperial dynasty he held four commands: Lu, Yan, Bin, and Fu.
units.literal: Serving the imperial dynasty, he held four commands: Lu, Yan, Bin, and Fu.

units.zh: 張礪，字夢臣，磁州滏陽人也。
units.en: Zhang Li, courtesy name Mengchen, was a native of Fuyang in Cizhou.
units.literal: Zhang Li, courtesy name Mengchen, was a man of Fuyang in Cizhou.

units.zh: 祖慶，父寶，世為農。
units.en: His grandfather Qing and his father Bao had been farmers for generations.
units.literal: His grandfather was Qing; his father Bao; for generations they were farmers.

units.zh: 礪幼嗜學，有文藻。
units.en: From youth Li loved learning and showed literary talent.
units.literal: Li from youth loved learning and had literary talent.

units.zh: 在布衣時，或睹民間爭競，必為親詣公府，辨其曲直，其負氣也如此。
units.en: While still a commoner, whenever he saw local disputes he would go in person to the magistrate's office to argue right from wrong. Such was his proud spirit.
units.literal: While still a commoner, whenever he saw disputes among the people he would personally go to the government offices to argue right and wrong—such was his proud spirit.

units.zh: 唐同光初，擢進士第，尋拜左拾遺，直史館。
units.en: At the beginning of the Tang Tongguang era he passed the jinshi examination and was soon appointed Left Remonstrator with duty in the History Office.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang in Tang he passed the jinshi examination and soon was appointed Left Remonstrator and duty officer in the History Office.

units.zh: 會郭崇韜伐蜀，奏請礪掌軍書。
units.en: When Guo Chongtao campaigned against Shu, he memorialized asking that Li manage military documents.
units.literal: When Guo Chongtao campaigned against Shu, he memorialized requesting Li to manage military documents.

units.zh: 蜀平，崇韜為魏王繼岌所誅，時崇韜左右親信皆懼禍奔逃，惟礪詣魏王府第，慟哭久之，時人皆服其高義。
units.en: When Shu was pacified, Chongtao was executed by Prince of Wei Jiji. Chongtao's close followers all fled in fear, but Li alone went to the prince's residence and wept long and bitterly. People of the time admired his loyalty.
units.literal: When Shu was pacified, Chongtao was executed by Prince of Wei Jiji; at that time Chongtao's close followers all feared disaster and fled, but only Li went to the Prince of Wei's residence and wept bitterly for a long time—people of the time all admired his lofty righteousness.

units.zh: 及魏王班師，礪從副招討使任圜東歸。
units.en: When the Prince of Wei withdrew, Li followed Deputy Pacification Commissioner Ren Yuan eastward.
units.literal: When the Prince of Wei withdrew his army, Li followed the deputy pacification commissioner Ren Yuan east in return.

units.zh: 至利州，會康延孝叛，回據漢州，圜奉魏王命，回軍西討延孝。
units.en: At Lizhou they learned that Kang Yanxiao had rebelled and seized Hanzhou. Yuan, on the prince's orders, turned the army west to attack him.
units.literal: Reaching Lizhou, it happened that Kang Yanxiao rebelled and turned back to hold Hanzhou; Yuan, following the Prince of Wei's command, turned the army west to attack Yanxiao.

units.zh: 時礪獻謀於圜，請伏精兵於後，先以羸師誘之，圜深以為然。
units.en: Li then offered Yuan a plan: hide elite troops in the rear and first lure the enemy with a weak force. Yuan strongly approved.
units.literal: At that time Li offered a plan to Yuan, asking to hide elite troops in the rear and first use a weak force to lure the enemy; Yuan deeply approved.

units.zh: 延孝本驍將也，任圜乃儒生也，延孝聞圜至，又睹其羸師，殊不介意，及戰酣，圜發精兵以擊之，延孝果敗，遂擒之以歸。
units.en: Yanxiao was a fierce general; Yuan was a scholar. When Yanxiao saw Yuan's weak vanguard he paid no heed. When the battle grew hot, Yuan unleashed his elite troops, broke Yanxiao, and brought him back captive.
units.literal: Yanxiao was originally a fierce general, while Yuan was a scholar; when Yanxiao heard Yuan had arrived and also saw his weak troops, he paid no attention at all; when the battle grew fierce Yuan unleashed elite troops to strike him, Yanxiao was indeed defeated, and they captured him and returned.

units.zh: 是歲四月五日至鳳翔，內官向延嗣奉莊宗命，令誅延孝。
units.en: On the fifth day of the fourth month they reached Fengxiang. Inner attendant Xiang Yansi, on Zhuangzong's orders, commanded Yanxiao's execution.
units.literal: On the fifth day of the fourth month of that year they reached Fengxiang; the inner attendant Xiang Yansi, following Emperor Zhuangzong's command, ordered Yanxiao executed.

units.zh: 監軍李延襲已聞洛中有變，故留延孝，且害任圜之功故也。
units.en: Army supervisor Li Yanxi had heard of trouble in Luoyang and therefore kept Yanxiao alive, partly to diminish Ren Yuan's merit.
units.literal: The army supervisor Li Yanxi had already heard there was trouble in Luoyang and therefore kept Yanxiao alive, also to harm Ren Yuan's merit.

units.zh: 圜未決，礪謂圜曰：「此賊構亂，遂致凱旋差晚，且明公血戰擒賊，安得違詔養禍，是破檻放虎，自貽其咎也。
units.en: Yuan hesitated. Li said to him: "This rebel stirred trouble and delayed our return. You fought in blood to capture him—how can you disobey the edict and keep this threat alive? That is breaking the cage and releasing the tiger.
units.literal: Yuan had not decided; Li said to Yuan, "This bandit stirred rebellion and thus made our triumphant return somewhat late; moreover, my lord fought in blood to capture the bandit—how can you disobey the edict and nurture disaster? That is breaking the cage and releasing the tiger, bringing calamity on yourself.

units.zh: 公若不決，余自殺此賊。」
units.en: If you will not decide, I will kill him myself."
units.literal: If my lord will not decide, I myself will kill this bandit."

units.zh: 任圜不得已，遂誅延孝。
units.en: Ren Yuan had no choice and executed Yanxiao.
units.literal: Ren Yuan had no choice and then executed Yanxiao.

units.zh: 天成初，明宗知其名，召為翰林學士。
units.en: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Mingzong knew his name and summoned him as Hanlin academician.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng Emperor Mingzong knew his name and summoned him as Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 再丁父母憂，服闋，皆復入為學士，歷禮部、兵部員外郎、知制誥充職。
units.en: Twice he mourned his parents. When each mourning ended he returned as academician and served as vice director in the Ministries of Rites and War and as drafter of imperial documents.
units.literal: Twice he observed mourning for his parents; when mourning ended he returned each time as academician, serving as Vice Director in the Ministries of Rites and War and as drafter of imperial documents.

units.zh: 未幾，父之妾卒。
units.en: Before long his father's concubine died.
units.literal: Before long his father's concubine died.

units.zh: 初，妾在世，礪以久侍先人，頗亦敬奉，諸幼子亦以祖母呼之。
units.en: While she lived, Li had respected her for long service to his late father, and the younger sons called her grandmother.
units.literal: Earlier, while the concubine was alive, Li because she had long served his late father also treated her with respect, and the younger sons likewise called her grandmother.

units.zh: 及卒，礪疑其事，詢於同僚，未有以對，礪即托故歸於滏陽，閑居三年，不行其服，論情制宜，識者韙之。
units.en: When she died Li was uncertain what mourning was proper and asked his colleagues, but none could answer. He pleaded illness, returned to Fuyang, and lived in retirement for three years without observing mourning. Judging sentiment and adapting to circumstance, the discerning approved.
units.literal: When she died Li was uncertain about the mourning obligation and asked his colleagues; none had an answer; Li then pleaded illness and returned to Fuyang, living in retirement for three years without observing mourning dress; judging sentiment and adapting to circumstance, the discerning approved him.

units.zh: 清泰中，復授尚書比部郎中、知制誥，依前充學士。
units.en: During Qingtai he was again appointed director in the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau and drafter of imperial documents, continuing as Hanlin academician.
units.literal: In the Qingtai era he was again appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau and drafter of imperial documents, continuing as before in the Hanlin Academy.

units.zh: 高祖起於晉陽，唐末帝命趙延壽進討，又命翰林學士和凝與延壽偕行。
units.en: When Gaozu rose at Jinyang, the last Tang emperor ordered Zhao Yanshou to advance against him and also ordered Hanlin academician He Ning to accompany Yanshou.
units.literal: When Gaozu rose at Jinyang, the last Tang emperor ordered Zhao Yanshou to advance in attack and also ordered the Hanlin academician He Ning to go with Yanshou.

units.zh: 礪素輕凝，慮不能集事，因自請行，唐末帝慰而許之。
units.en: Li had always looked down on Ning and feared he could not manage the task, so he asked to go himself. The last Tang emperor comforted him and agreed.
units.literal: Li had always looked down on Ning and feared he could not bring affairs together, so he requested to go himself; the last Tang emperor comforted him and granted it.

units.zh: 及唐軍敗於團柏谷，與延壽俱陷於契丹，契丹以舊職縻之，累官至吏部尚書。
units.en: When the Tang army was defeated at Tuanbai Valley he fell into Khitan hands with Yanshou. The Khitan kept him in his former office and he eventually rose to Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: When the Tang army was defeated at Tuanbai Valley he fell into Khitan hands together with Yanshou; the Khitan held him with his former office and he rose in rank to Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 契丹入汴，授右僕射、平章事、集賢殿大學士，隨至鎮州。
units.en: When the Khitan entered Bian he was appointed Right Vice Director, Grand Councilor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and followed on to Zhenzhou.
units.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian he was appointed Right Vice Director, Grand Councilor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and followed on to Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 會契丹主卒，永康王北去，蕭翰自東京過常山，乃引鐵騎圍其第。
units.en: When the Khitan ruler died, Prince Yongkang went north. Xiao Han came from the Eastern Capital past Changshan and led iron cavalry to surround Li's residence.
units.literal: It happened that the Khitan ruler died and Prince Yongkang went north; Xiao Han came from the Eastern Capital past Changshan and then led iron cavalry to surround his residence.

units.zh: 時礪有疾，方伏枕，翰見礪責之曰：「爾言於先帝，雲不得任蕃人作節度使，如此則社稷不永矣；
units.en: Li was then ill in bed. When Han saw him he reproached him: "You told the late emperor that barbarians must not be made military governors, or the altars of state would not long endure;
units.literal: At that time Li was ill and lying on his pillow; when Han saw him he reproached Li, saying, "You told the late emperor that barbarians must not be made military governors—if so the altars of state will not long endure;

units.zh: 又先帝來時，令我於汴州大內安下，爾言不可；
units.en: when the late emperor came you said I could not lodge in the great inner palace at Bianzhou;
units.literal: moreover when the late emperor came he ordered me to lodge in the great inner palace at Bianzhou and you said it could not be done;

units.zh: 又我為汴州節度使，爾在中書，何故行帖與我？」
units.en: and I am military governor of Bianzhou while you sit in the Secretariat—why send me official correspondence?"
units.literal: moreover I am military governor of Bianzhou and you are in the Secretariat—why send me official correspondence?"

units.zh: 礪抗聲而對，辭氣不屈，翰遂鎖礪而去。
units.en: Li answered in a loud voice without yielding. Han shackled him and left.
units.literal: Li answered in a loud voice, his tone unbending; Han then shackled Li and left.

units.zh: 〈（《遼史》：礪抗聲曰：「此國家大體，安危所系，吾實言之。
units.en: (Liao History: Li answered loudly: "This concerns the great principle of the state and what binds safety and peril. I spoke truthfully.
units.literal: (Liao History: Li answered loudly, saying, "This concerns the great principle of the state and what binds safety and peril—I spoke truthfully.

units.zh: 欲殺即殺，奚以鎖為！」）〉
units.en: If you wish to kill me, then kill—why shackle me!")〉
units.literal: If you wish to kill, then kill—why shackle me!")〉

units.zh: 鎮州節度使滿達勒尋解其鎖，是夜以疾卒，家人燼其骨，歸葬於滏陽。
units.en: Military Governor Mandale of Zhenzhou soon released his shackles. That night Li died of illness. His family cremated his bones and buried them at Fuyang.
units.literal: The military governor of Zhenzhou Mandale soon released his shackles; that night he died of illness; his family cremated his bones and returned them for burial at Fuyang.

units.zh: 礪素耿直，嗜酒無檢。
units.en: Li was by nature upright and blunt, fond of wine and without restraint.
units.literal: Li was by nature upright and blunt, fond of wine and without restraint.

units.zh: 始陷契丹時，曾背契丹南歸，為追騎所獲，契丹主怒曰：「爾何舍我而去？」
units.en: When he first fell into Khitan hands he once fled south, was captured by pursuers, and the Khitan ruler angrily said, "Why did you abandon me?"
units.literal: When he first fell into Khitan hands he once turned his back on the Khitan and fled south, was captured by pursuing horsemen, and the Khitan ruler angrily said, "Why did you abandon me and leave?"

units.zh: 礪曰：「礪，漢人也，衣服飲食與此不同，生不如死，請速就刃。」
units.en: Li said, "I am a Han man. Clothing and food here are not the same. Life is worse than death. Grant me the blade at once."
units.literal: Li said, "Li is a Han man; clothing and food here are not the same—life is worse than death; please quickly grant the blade."

units.zh: 契丹主顧通事高唐英曰：「我常戒爾輩善待此人，致其逃去，過在爾輩。」
units.en: The Khitan ruler turned to interpreter Gao Tangying and said, "I often warned you to treat this man well, yet he escaped. The fault is yours."
units.literal: The Khitan ruler turned to the interpreter Gao Tangying and said, "I often warned you all to treat this man well, yet he escaped—the fault lies with you."

units.zh: 因笞唐英一百，其為契丹主善待也如此。
units.en: He had Tangying flogged one hundred strokes. Such was the favor the Khitan ruler showed him.
units.literal: He then flogged Tangying one hundred strokes—such was how the Khitan ruler favored and treated him.

units.zh: 礪平生抱義憐才，急於獎拔，聞人之善，必攘袂以稱之，見人之貧，亦倒篋以濟之，故死之之日，中朝士大夫亦皆嘆惜焉。
units.en: Throughout his life Li embraced righteousness and pitied talent, eager to promote others. Hearing of someone's excellence he would praise it openly; seeing poverty he would empty his purse to help. On the day of his death the scholar-officials of the central court all sighed in regret.
units.literal: Throughout his life Li embraced righteousness and pitied talent, eager to promote others; hearing of someone's excellence he would roll up his sleeves and praise it; seeing someone's poverty he would empty his purse to aid them—therefore on the day of his death the scholar-officials of the central court also all sighed in regret.

units.zh: 蕭翰者，契丹諸部之長也。
units.en: Xiao Han was a chief among the Khitan tribes.
units.literal: Xiao Han was a chief of the various Khitan tribes.

units.zh: 父曰阿缽。
units.en: His father was named Abo.
units.literal: His father was named Abo.

units.zh: 劉仁恭鎮幽州，阿巴曾引眾寇平州，仁恭遣驍將劉雁郎與其子守光率五百騎先守其州，阿缽不知，為郡人所紿，因赴牛酒之會，為守光所擒。
units.en: When Liu Rengong governed Youzhou, Abo once raided Pingzhou. Rengong sent the fierce general Liu Yanlang and his son Shouguang with five hundred horsemen to hold the prefecture. Abo did not know this, was deceived by the locals, attended a feast of meat and wine, and was captured by Shouguang.
units.literal: When Liu Rengong governed Youzhou, Abo once led a host to raid Pingzhou; Rengong sent the fierce general Liu Yanlang and his son Shouguang with five hundred horsemen to hold the prefecture first; Abo did not know this, was deceived by the prefectural people, went to a feast of ox and wine, and was captured by Shouguang.

units.zh: 契丹請贖之，仁恭許其請，尋歸。
units.en: The Khitan requested his ransom. Rengong agreed and Abo soon returned.
units.literal: The Khitan requested his ransom; Rengong granted the request and he soon returned.

units.zh: 阿巴妹為安巴堅妻，則德光之母也。
units.en: Abo's younger sister was wife to Ambajian and mother of Deguang.
units.literal: Abo's younger sister was wife to Ambajian, who was the mother of Deguang.

units.zh: 翰有妹，亦嫁於德光，故國人謂翰為國舅。
units.en: Han also had a sister who married Deguang, so his people called him the imperial uncle by marriage.
units.literal: Han also had a younger sister who married Deguang; therefore the people of the state called Han the imperial uncle by marriage.

units.zh: 契丹入東京，以翰為宣武軍節度使。
units.en: When the Khitan entered the Eastern Capital they made Han military governor of Xuanwu.
units.literal: When the Khitan entered the Eastern Capital they made Han military governor of the Xuanwu army.

units.zh: 契丹比無姓氏，翰將有節度之命，乃以蕭為姓，翰為名，自是翰之一族皆稱姓蕭。
units.en: The Khitan had not used surnames. When Han was to receive a command appointment he took Xiao as surname and Han as given name, and thereafter his whole clan bore the surname Xiao.
units.literal: The Khitan had not had surnames in the past; when Han was about to receive a commandery appointment he took Xiao as surname and Han as given name, and from then on Han's whole clan were called surname Xiao.

units.zh: 契丹主北去，留翰以鎮河南。
units.en: When the Khitan ruler went north he left Han to garrison the lands south of the river.
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler went north he left Han to garrison the lands south of the river.

units.zh: 時漢高祖已建號於太原，翰懼，將北歸，慮京師無主，則眾皆為亂，乃遣蕃騎至洛京迎唐明宗幼子許王從益知南朝軍國事。
units.en: Han Gaozu had already established his title at Taiyuan. Xiao Han feared and meant to return north, worried that without a ruler in the capital the people would riot. He sent Khitan horsemen to Luoyang to welcome Mingzong's young son Prince Xu Congyi to provisionally manage the southern dynasty's affairs.
units.literal: At that time Han Gaozu had already established his title at Taiyuan; Han was afraid and was about to return north, fearing that if the capital had no ruler the masses would all turn to chaos; he therefore sent Khitan horsemen to Luoyang to welcome Tang Emperor Mingzong's young son, Prince Xu Congyi, to provisionally manage the southern dynasty's military and state affairs.

units.zh: 從益至，翰率蕃將拜於殿上。
units.en: When Congyi arrived, Han led the Khitan generals to bow in the hall.
units.literal: When Congyi arrived, Han led the Khitan generals to bow in the hall.

units.zh: 翌日，翰乃輦其寶貨鞍轡而北。
units.en: The next day Han carted his treasures, saddles, and bridles north.
units.literal: The next day Han carted his treasures, saddles, and bridles north.

units.zh: 漢人以許王既立，不復為亂，果中其狡計。
units.en: The Han people, seeing Prince Xu established, no longer rioted. His cunning plan had succeeded.
units.literal: The Han people, seeing Prince Xu already established, no longer made trouble—his cunning plan indeed succeeded.

units.zh: 翰行至鎮州，遇張礪，翰以舊事致忿，就第數其失而鎖之。
units.en: At Zhenzhou Han encountered Zhang Li. Resentful over old matters, he came to Li's residence, recounted his faults, and shackled him.
units.literal: When Han reached Zhenzhou he encountered Zhang Li; Han, resentful over old matters, came to his residence, recounted his faults, and shackled him.

units.zh: 翰歸本國，為永康王烏裕所鎖，尋卒於本土。
units.en: When Han returned home he was shackled by Prince Yongkang Wuyu and soon died in Khitan territory.
units.literal: When Han returned to his own state he was shackled by Prince Yongkang Wuyu and soon died in his homeland.

units.zh: 劉晞者，涿州人也。
units.en: Liu Xi was a native of Zhuozhou.
units.literal: Liu Xi was a man of Zhuozhou.

units.zh: 父濟雍，累為本郡諸邑令長。
units.en: His father Jiyong had served successively as magistrate of various districts in the commandery.
units.literal: His father Jiyong successively served as magistrate or chief of various districts in the native commandery.

units.zh: 晞少以儒學稱於鄉里，嘗為唐將周德威從事，後陷於契丹，契丹以漢職縻之。
units.en: From youth Xi was famed in his district for classical learning. He once served on the staff of Tang general Zhou Dewei, later fell into Khitan hands, and the Khitan kept him in Han offices.
units.literal: Xi from youth was famed in his district for classical learning, once served as staff to the Tang general Zhou Dewei, later fell into Khitan hands, and the Khitan held him with Han offices.

units.zh: 天福中，契丹命晞為燕京留守，嘗於契丹三知貢舉，歷官至同平章事、兼侍中。
units.en: During Tianfu the Khitan appointed Xi regent of Yanjing. He thrice oversaw the civil service examinations under the Khitan and rose to Grand Councilor and concurrent Vice Grand Counselor.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era the Khitan appointed Xi regent of Yanjing; he thrice oversaw the civil service examinations under the Khitan and rose in office to Grand Councilor of the Same Rank and concurrent Vice Grand Counselor.

units.zh: 隨契丹入汴，授洛京留守。
units.en: He followed the Khitan into Bian and was appointed regent of the Luoyang capital.
units.literal: Following the Khitan into Bian he was appointed regent of the Luoyang capital.

units.zh: 會河陽軍亂，晞走許州，又奔東京，蕭翰遣兵援晞至洛下。
units.en: When the Heyang army rebelled, Xi fled to Xuzhou and then to the Eastern Capital. Xiao Han sent troops to support him at Luoyang.
units.literal: It happened that the Heyang army rebelled; Xi fled to Xuzhou and then ran to the Eastern Capital; Xiao Han sent troops to aid Xi down to Luoyang.

units.zh: 契丹主死，晞自洛復至東京，隨蕭翰北歸，遂留鎮州。
units.en: When the Khitan ruler died, Xi returned from Luoyang to the Eastern Capital, followed Xiao Han north, and remained at Zhenzhou.
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler died, Xi went from Luoyang back to the Eastern Capital, followed Xiao Han north in return, and then remained at Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 漢初，與滿達勒同奔定州，後卒於北蕃。
units.en: At the beginning of Han he fled with Mandale to Dingzhou and later died in the north.
units.literal: At the beginning of Han he fled with Mandale to Dingzhou and later died in the northern barbarian lands.

units.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》：劉珂，晞之子也，尚世宗妹燕國公主。）〉
units.en: (Khitan State Chronicle: Liu Ke was Xi's son and married Emperor Shizong's younger sister, Princess of Yan.)〉
units.literal: (Khitan State Chronicle: Liu Ke was Xi's son and married the Shizong emperor's younger sister, Princess of Yan.)〉

units.zh: 崔廷勛，不知何許人也。
units.en: Cui Tingxun was a man of unknown origin.
units.literal: Cui Tingxun—it is not known whence he came.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒註》引宋白曰：廷勛本河內人。）〉
units.en: (Zizhi Tongjian commentary citing Song Bai: Tingxun was originally from Henei.)〉
units.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian commentary citing Song Bai: Tingxun was originally a man of Henei.)〉

units.zh: 形貌魁偉，美須髯。
units.en: He was tall and imposing, with a handsome beard.
units.literal: His form was tall and imposing and his beard and whiskers handsome.

units.zh: 幼陷契丹，歷仕至雲州節度使，官至侍中。
units.en: He fell into Khitan hands in youth, rose to military governor of Yunzhou, and reached Vice Grand Counselor.
units.literal: He fell into Khitan hands in youth, served through offices up to military governor of Yunzhou, and reached the rank of Vice Grand Counselor.

units.zh: 契丹入汴，遷少帝於封禪寺，遣廷勛以兵防守，尋授河陽節度使，甚得民情。
units.en: When the Khitan entered Bian they moved Emperor Shaodi to Fengchan Temple and sent Tingxun with troops to guard him. Soon he was made military governor of Heyang and won great popular approval.
units.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian they moved Emperor Shaodi to Fengchan Temple and sent Tingxun with troops to guard him; soon he was appointed military governor of Heyang and greatly won popular sentiment.

units.zh: 契丹北行，武行德率軍趨河陽，廷勛為行德所逐，乃與奚王伊剌保懷州，尋以兵反攻行德，行德出戰，為廷勛所敗。
units.en: When the Khitan marched north, Wu Xingde led troops toward Heyang. Tingxun was driven off and joined the Xi king Yila in holding Huaizhou. He soon counterattacked Xingde, who came out to fight and was defeated.
units.literal: When the Khitan marched north, Wu Xingde led troops toward Heyang; Tingxun was driven off by Xingde and then joined the Xi king Yila in holding Huaizhou; soon he counterattacked Xingde with troops; Xingde came out to fight and was defeated by Tingxun.

units.zh: 及契丹主死，遂歸鎮州。
units.en: When the Khitan ruler died he returned to Zhenzhou.
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler died he then returned to Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 漢初，與麻達勒同奔定州，後沒於北蕃。
units.en: At the beginning of Han he fled with Madale to Dingzhou and later perished in the north.
units.literal: At the beginning of Han he fled with Madale to Dingzhou and later perished in the northern barbarian lands.

units.zh: 史臣曰：帝王之尊，必由天命。
units.en: The historian comments: The exalted dignity of emperors and kings must come through Heaven's mandate.
units.literal: The historian says: The exalted dignity of emperors and kings must come through Heaven's mandate.

units.zh: 雖韓信、彭越之勇，吳濞、淮南之勢，猶不可以妄冀，而況二安之庸昧，相輔為亂，固宜其自取滅亡也。
units.en: Even men with the courage of Han Xin and Peng Yue or the power of Wu Pi and Huainan may not vainly hope for the throne—how much less the mediocrity of the two Ans, aiding each other in rebellion. It is fitting they destroyed themselves.
units.literal: Even with the courage of Han Xin and Peng Yue, the power of Wu Pi and Huainan, one still may not vainly hope—how much more so the mediocrity and dullness of the two Ans, aiding each other in rebellion: it is fitting they brought destruction on themselves.

units.zh: 後之擁強兵蒞重鎮者，得不以為鑒乎！
units.en: Those who later hold strong armies and weighty commands—can they fail to take this as a warning!
units.literal: Those who later hold strong armies and come to weighty commands—can they fail to take this as a mirror!

units.zh: 彥澤狼子野心，盈貫而死，晚矣！
units.en: Yanze had the heart of a wolf cub. He died only when his crimes were full—too late!
units.literal: Yanze had the heart of a wolf cub; he died only when his crimes were full—too late!

units.zh: 德鈞諸人，與晉事相終始，故附見於茲焉。
units.en: Dejun and the others were bound up with Jin affairs from beginning to end; therefore they are appended here.
units.literal: Dejun and the others were involved with Jin affairs from beginning to end; therefore they are appended here.

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

findings.problem: The source phrase 梁開平初 (early Kaiping) is flattened to the entire AD 907–911 Kaiping era. This erases the explicit early-phase qualifier and makes each localized capture or adoption look possible throughout the whole reign.
findings.action: Replace the whole-era interval and dependent hints with the conservative early-Kaiping phase AD 907–908, retaining 梁開平初 and the individual event wording.

findings.problem: 明宗即位 names the accession event itself, but the record turns it into a service interval through the end of Mingzong’s reign (AD 926–933).
findings.action: Use the accession-year AD 926 for the return of Zhao Dejun’s surname and recompute the dependent active-date hint; do not present the event as continuous service through AD 933.

findings.problem: These combined attestations include the later review of An Chongrong’s head and Du Chongwei’s later beheading of him, but retain only the AD 941 rebellion date. The cited sequence crosses the post-rebellion completion into the next Western year.
findings.action: Preserve the Chinese sequence and replace the single AD 941 point with a source-faithful AD 941–942 interval or separate correctly bounded temporal contexts; recompute only any dependent hint that changes.

findings.problem: The extraction treats the Kaiyun 3 late-winter/capital-occupation sequence as a flat AD 946 point even where the cited event follows the twelfth-month entry into Bian and belongs to the cross-year 946–947 sequence. Several dependent hints already preserve AD 947, exposing the claim-level mismatch.
findings.action: Retain the Chinese Kaiyun wording and use a proleptic-Gregorian conversion or conservative AD 946–947 interval for cross-year winter events; use AD 947 where the source sequence is explicitly after the capital entry. Recompute active-date hints from the repaired claims.

findings.problem: These kinship and title attestations supply no dated local event in the cited chapter, but are given imported before/reign-wide Western chronology. A parent, spouse, or ruler-name reference is not evidence that the relation or subject was active throughout an inferred reign.
findings.action: Keep the relationships and title/name attestations, but make them explicitly undated source evidence and clear the dependent active-date hints unless a separately pinned source supports a temporal endpoint.

findings.problem: The historian’s comparison and editorial appendix are retrospective discourse, not dated local events. Imported Early Han and Jing-era dates, a synthetic AD 946 judgment date, and a Qingtai–Tianfu span incorrectly turn allusions and commentary into personal activity.
findings.action: Retain the retrospective-reference records and editorial text as explicitly undated attestations; remove unsupported Western date containers and dependent active-date hints unless separately pinned chronology is added.

findings.problem: The Song Bai editorial-note attestation correctly declares unresolved chronology, so it cannot be approved. Its active-date hint remains a research-required hold rather than source-supported personal chronology.
findings.action: Preserve the exact unresolved source attestation and research-required hint; obtain and pin independent chronology for Song Bai before a future approval, without guessing a floruit.
